claims.summary: Any company may apply for recognition or annual renewal of such recognition as an alien reinsurer, provided it is licensed to write reinsurance by, and has its head office or domicile in, a non-U.S. jurisdiction that is recognized by a U.S. state as a Qualified Jurisdiction or as a Reciprocal Jurisdiction, provided that the Reciprocal Jurisdiction is not party to an in-force Covered Agreement as described in paragraph (i) of this section.

claims.quote: To obtain such recognition, the company must submit to Treasury the fee in accordance with the provisions of
claims.summary: To obtain such recognition, the company must submit to Treasury the fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.

claims.quote: Be recognized by at least one U.S. state as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or a “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer,” as defined by the state's credit for reinsurance law or regulation based on the NAIC's Credit for Reinsurance Model Law and Regulation, and submit proof of such recognition;
claims.summary: The party must be recognized by at least one U.S. state as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or a “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer,” as defined by the state's credit for reinsurance law or regulation based on the NAIC's Credit for Reinsurance Model Law and Regulation, and submit proof of such recognition.

claims.quote: Meet and maintain all capital and surplus, market conduct, and other requirements for eligibility as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer” in accordance with the law and regulation of all U.S. states granting it such recognition;
claims.summary: The party must meet and maintain all capital and surplus, market conduct, and other requirements for eligibility as an “Accredited Reinsurer,” “Certified Reinsurer,” or “Reciprocal Jurisdiction Reinsurer” in accordance with the law and regulation of all U.S. states granting it such recognition.

claims.quote: Submit to Treasury: (i) For initial applications for recognition, all information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the two most recently completed calendar years. (ii) For applications for renewal of such recognition, all annual filing information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the most recently completed calendar year. (iii) Payment of the application fee in accordance with the provisions of
claims.summary: The party must submit to Treasury: (i) For initial applications for recognition, all information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the two most recently completed calendar years; (ii) For applications for renewal of such recognition, all annual filing information provided to any U.S. state regulator in the most recently completed calendar year; (iii) Payment of the application fee in accordance with the provisions of § 223.22.

claims.quote: Treasury determines the amount of paid-up capital and surplus of any company holding or seeking a certificate of authority or recognized (or seeking recognition) as an admitted reinsurer pursuant to § 223.12(h) on an insurance accounting basis under the regulations in this part, from the company's financial statements and other information, or by such examination of the company at its own expense as Treasury may deem appropriate.
claims.summary: Treasury determines the amount of paid-up capital and surplus of any company holding or seeking a certificate of authority or recognized (or seeking recognition) as an admitted reinsurer pursuant to § 223.12(h) on an insurance accounting basis under the regulations in this part, from the company's financial statements and other information, or by such examination of the company at its own expense as Treasury may deem appropriate.

claims.quote: A list of certificate holding companies is published annually as of August 1 in Department Circular No. 570, Companies Holding Certificates of Authority as Acceptable Sureties on Federal Bonds and as Acceptable Reinsuring Companies, with information as to underwriting limitations, areas in which listed sureties are licensed to transact surety business, and other details.
claims.summary: A list of certificate holding companies must be published annually as of August 1 in Department Circular No. 570.

claims.quote: If Treasury shall take any exceptions to the financial statements submitted by a company or other information pertinent to the company's financial solvency, before issuing Department Circular 570, Treasury shall give a company due notice of such exceptions.
claims.summary: Treasury must give a company due notice of any exceptions to the financial statements or other information pertinent to the company's financial solvency before issuing Department Circular 570.

claims.affected_party: principals required to furnish the bond
claims.quote: Bonds underwritten by certified companies on the Department Circular No. 570 list may be presented to an agency bond-approving official for acceptance.
claims.summary: Bonds underwritten by certified companies on the Department Circular No. 570 list may be presented to an agency bond-approving official for acceptance.

claims.quote: Selection of a particular qualified company from among all companies holding certificates of authority is discretionary with the principal required to furnish the bond, but the acceptance of a bond by an agency bond-approving official is subject to
claims.summary: The acceptance of a bond by an agency bond-approving official is subject to certain conditions.

claims.quote: An agency bond-approving official may decline to accept bonds underwritten by a certified company for cause, but only if the company has been given advance written notice by such agency.
claims.summary: An agency bond-approving official may decline to accept bonds underwritten by a certified company for cause, but only if the company has been given advance written notice.

claims.quote: The advance written notice shall: (i) State the intention of the agency to decline bonds underwritten by the company; (ii) State the reasons for or cause of the proposed declination of such bonds; (iii) Provide the company with an opportunity to rebut the stated reasons or cause; and (iv) Provide the company with an opportunity to cure the stated reasons or cause.
claims.summary: The advance written notice shall state the intention of the agency to decline bonds underwritten by the company, state the reasons for or cause of the proposed declination, provide the company with an opportunity to rebut the stated reasons or cause, and provide the company with an opportunity to cure the stated reasons or cause.

claims.quote: The agency may decline to accept bonds underwritten by the company if, after consideration of any submission by the company or failure of the company to respond to the agency's notice, the agency issues a written determination that the bonds should not be accepted, consistent with agency authorities.
claims.summary: The agency may decline to accept bonds underwritten by the company if, after consideration of any submission by the company or failure of the company to respond to the agency's notice, the agency issues a written determination that the bonds should not be accepted, consistent with agency authorities.

claims.quote: The agency shall articulate its procedures and for cause standards for declining to accept bonds in an agency regulation prior to declining any bonds in specific cases. The agency regulation should be subject to notice and comment rulemaking.
claims.summary: The agency shall articulate its procedures and for cause standards for declining to accept bonds in an agency regulation prior to declining any bonds in specific cases. The agency regulation should be subject to notice and comment rulemaking.

claims.quote: Agencies that decline bonds under this section are encouraged to use best efforts to ensure that persons conducting business with the agency are aware that bonds underwritten by the particular certified company will not be accepted.
claims.summary: Agencies that decline bonds under this section are encouraged to use best efforts to ensure that persons conducting business with the agency are aware that bonds underwritten by the particular certified company will not be accepted.

claims.quote: The agency's authority to decline bonds under this section does not apply: (i) When the underlying obligation or other for cause reason that forms the basis for the agency's written determination to decline bonds under paragraph (b)(2) of this section, or the agency written determination to decline bonds, has been stayed or enjoined by a court of competent jurisdiction, or (ii) To otherwise acceptable payment and performance contract bonds, when the agency has already accepted a project bid bond on a contract before making the written determination under paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
claims.summary: The agency's authority to decline bonds under this section does not apply when the underlying obligation or other for cause reason that forms the basis for the agency's written determination to decline bonds has been stayed or enjoined by a court of competent jurisdiction, or to otherwise acceptable payment and performance contract bonds when the agency has already accepted a project bid bond on a contract before making the written determination.

claims.quote: Notwithstanding any provision of this section, an agency bond-approving official may decline a bond from a Treasury-certified surety without advance notice if the bond is not executed in proper form, or is not in the correct penal sum amount, or is otherwise technically deficient on its face.
claims.summary: An agency bond-approving official may decline a bond from a Treasury-certified surety without advance notice if the bond is not executed in proper form, or is not in the correct penal sum amount, or is otherwise technically deficient on its face.

claims.quote: A revocation of a company's certificate of authority under § 223.19 or § 223.20 precludes the company from underwriting or reinsuring additional bonds for any agency, and therefore revokes the company's opportunity to have its bonds presented to any agency bond-approving official for acceptance.
claims.summary: A revocation of a company's certificate of authority precludes the company from underwriting or reinsuring additional bonds for any agency, and therefore revokes the company's opportunity to have its bonds presented to any agency bond-approving official for acceptance.

claims.quote: Whenever Treasury has reason to believe that a company is not complying with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 9304-9308 and/or the regulations under this part, including but not limited to a failure to satisfy corporate and financial standards, Treasury shall: (a) Notify the company of the facts or conduct which indicate such non-compliance, and provide the company an opportunity to respond, and (b) Revoke a company's certificate of authority after providing notice to the company if: (1) The company does not respond satisfactorily to Treasury's notification of non-compliance, or (2) The company responded, was provided an opportunity to demonstrate or achieve compliance, and failed to do so.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify a company of non-compliance and provide an opportunity to respond. If the company fails to respond satisfactorily or fails to achieve compliance after being given an opportunity, Treasury must revoke the company's certificate of authority.

claims.quote: If, after one year from the date that Treasury notifies the company of its decision to decline to renew or revoke the certificate of authority of a company under this part, the company can demonstrate that the basis for the non-renewal or revocation has been cured, as determined by Treasury in its discretion, and that it can comply with, and does meet, all continuing requirements for certification under 31 U.S.C. 9304-9308 and this part, the company may submit an application to Treasury for reinstatement or reissuance of a certificate of authority, which will be granted without prejudice if all such requirements are met.
claims.summary: A company may submit an application to Treasury for reinstatement or reissuance of a certificate of authority if it can demonstrate that the basis for non-renewal or revocation has been cured and it meets all continuing requirements.

claims.quote: Treasury may waive the one year waiting period for good cause shown, as determined by Treasury in its sole discretion.
claims.summary: Treasury may waive the one-year waiting period for reinstatement if good cause is shown.

claims.quote: Fees shall be imposed and collected, for the services listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section that are performed by Treasury, regardless of whether the action requested is granted or denied.
claims.summary: Fees shall be imposed and collected for the services listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section, regardless of whether the action requested is granted or denied.

claims.quote: In a given year a uniform fee will be collected from every company requesting a particular category of service, e.g., determination of a company's continuing qualifications for annual renewal of its certificate of authority. However, Treasury reserves the right to redetermine the amounts of fees annually.
claims.summary: A uniform fee will be collected from every company requesting a particular category of service, but Treasury reserves the right to redetermine the amounts of fees annually.

claims.quote: Fees are determined in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-25, as amended.
claims.summary: Fees are determined in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-25, as amended.

claims.quote: Specific fee information may be obtained from the Surety Bonds Program, or online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/surety-bonds/user-fees.pdf.
claims.summary: Specific fee information may be obtained from the Surety Bonds Program or online at the provided URL.

claims.quote: In addition, a notice of the amount of a fee referred to in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section will be published in the Federal Register as each change in such fee is made.
claims.summary: A notice of the amount of a fee referred to in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section will be published in the Federal Register as each change in such fee is made.

document_title: 31 CFR Part 223 (point-in-time 2026-07-01)

category: Title 31 — Code of Federal Regulations parts

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may enter into a reciprocal agreement with a State for the collection of past-due support being enforced by the State by administrative offset from certain Federal payments.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must enter into reciprocal agreements with States for the collection of past-due support being enforced by the State through administrative offset.

claims.affected_party: disbursing officials of Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials of the United States
claims.quote: Upon notification of past-due support either directly from a State which has entered into such an agreement or from HHS, disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official of the United States shall offset Federal payments which are subject to offset under this section, to collect past-due support.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must offset Federal payments subject to offset under this section to collect past-due support upon notification from a State or HHS.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may enter into reciprocal agreements with States for disbursing officials of Fiscal Service and any other Federal disbursing official to offset certain Federal payments to collect past-due support being enforced by the State.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must enter into reciprocal agreements with States for disbursing officials to offset Federal payments to collect past-due support being enforced by the State.

claims.quote: States notifying Fiscal Service of past-due support must do so in the manner and format prescribed by Fiscal Service. States notifying HHS of past-due support must do so in the manner and format prescribed by HHS.
claims.summary: States must notify Fiscal Service or HHS of past-due support in the manner and format prescribed by Fiscal Service or HHS.

claims.quote: The notification of past-due support must be accompanied by a certification that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the State has complied with all the requirements as set forth in paragraph (h) of this section and with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure.
claims.summary: States must accompany the notification of past-due support with a certification that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that all requirements have been met.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will reject a notification of past-due support where the past-due support owed is less than $25.00.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must reject notifications of past-due support where the amount owed is less than $25.00.

claims.quote: Debts properly submitted to Fiscal Service for administrative offset will remain subject to collection by administrative offset until withdrawn by the State provided the debt remains past-due and legally enforceable.
claims.summary: States must ensure that debts remain subject to collection by administrative offset until withdrawn, provided the debt remains past-due and legally enforceable.

claims.quote: The State notifying Fiscal Service or HHS of past-due support shall, in the manner and in the time frames provided by Fiscal Service or HHS, notify Fiscal Service or HHS of deletions or decreases in the amount of a debt referred for collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: States must notify Fiscal Service or HHS of deletions or decreases in the amount of a debt referred for collection by administrative offset in the manner and time frames provided.

claims.quote: The State, or Fiscal Service or HHS on behalf of the State, if the State requests and Fiscal Service or HHS agrees, shall send a written notification, at least 30 days in advance of referral of the debt for offset, to the individual owing past-due support, informing the individual that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by administrative offset against Federal payments.
claims.summary: The State, or Fiscal Service or HHS on behalf of the State, must send a written notification at least 30 days in advance to the individual owing past-due support, informing them of the intent to refer the debt for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: Prior to referring a debt to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset, States must provide individuals with a reasonable opportunity to exercise the rights enumerated in paragraph (h)(1) of this section in accordance with procedures prescribed by the State.
claims.summary: States must provide individuals with a reasonable opportunity to exercise their rights enumerated in paragraph (h)(1) of this section before referring a debt to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: Federal payments subject to offset under this section include all Federal payments except: (1) Payments due to an individual under (i) Title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965; (ii) The Social Security Act; (iii) Part B of the Black Lung Benefits Act; (iv) Any law administered by the Railroad Retirement Board; (2) Payments which the Secretary determines are exempt from offset in accordance with paragraph (k) of this section; (3) Payments from which collection of past-due support by administrative offset is expressly prohibited by law; (4) Payments made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (except that tax refund payments are subject to offset under separate authority); and (5) Payments made under the tariff laws of the United States.
claims.summary: Federal disbursing officials must ensure that payments subject to offset under this section include all Federal payments except those specified in the regulation.

claims.quote: Unless a lower maximum offset limitation is provided by applicable State law, the maximum part of a Federal salary payment per pay period subject to offset to collect past-due support shall not exceed those amounts set forth at section 1673(b)(2) (A) and (B) of Title 15, United States Code.
claims.summary: Federal disbursing officials must ensure that the maximum part of a Federal salary payment per pay period subject to offset does not exceed the amounts set forth in Title 15, United States Code, unless a lower limit is provided by State law.

claims.quote: The disbursing official shall send written notice to the debtor of the maximum offset limitations described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section. The notice shall include a request that the debtor submit supporting affidavits or other documentation necessary to determine the applicable offset percentage limitation.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must send written notice to the debtor of the maximum offset limitations and request supporting documentation to determine the applicable offset percentage.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials of the Department of the Treasury, the Department of Defense, the United States Postal Service, or any other Government corporation, any disbursing official of the United States designated by the Secretary, or any disbursing official of an executive department or agency that disburses Federal payments shall offset payments subject to offset under this section to satisfy, in whole or part, a debt owed by the payee.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must offset payments subject to offset under this section to satisfy, in whole or part, a debt owed by the payee.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall compare payment certification records with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset. A match will occur when the taxpayer identifying number and name control of a payment record are the same as the taxpayer identifying number and name control of a debt record.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must compare payment certification records with debt records to determine if a match occurs.

claims.quote: When a match occurs and all other requirements for offset have been met, the disbursing official shall offset the payment to satisfy, in whole or part, the debt.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must offset the payment to satisfy, in whole or part, the debt when a match occurs and all other requirements have been met.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official which conducts an offset will notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy past-due support.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy past-due support.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official which conducts an offset under this section will share with HHS, upon request by the Secretary of HHS, information contained in payment certification records of persons who are delinquent in child support obligations that would assist in the collection of such debts.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must share information contained in payment certification records of persons who are delinquent in child support obligations with HHS upon request.

claims.quote: Neither the disbursing official nor the agency authorizing the payment shall be liable for the amount of the administrative offset on the basis that the underlying obligation, represented by the payment before the administrative offset was taken, was not satisfied.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials and payment agencies must not be liable for the amount of the administrative offset if the underlying obligation was not satisfied.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure that an individual's Social Security number is not visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail.

claims.affected_party: Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials
claims.quote: Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer administrative offset, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents for specific purposes, such as interoffice communications, notices, and responses to requests, but must generally redact them.

claims.quote: Past-due support will be collected by tax refund offset upon notification to Fiscal Service in accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), 42 U.S.C. 664 and this section.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must collect past-due support by tax refund offset upon notification in accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), 42 U.S.C. 664, and this section.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will compare tax refund payment records, as certified by the IRS, with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service. A match will occur when the taxpayer identifying number (as that term is used in 26 U.S.C. 6109) and name of a payment certification record are the same as the taxpayer identifying number and name of a delinquent debtor record. When a match occurs and all other requirements for tax refund offset have been met, Fiscal Service will reduce the amount of any tax refund payment payable to a debtor by the amount of any past-due support debt owed by the debtor.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must compare tax refund payment records with debt records, and if a match occurs and all requirements are met, reduce the tax refund payment by the amount of past-due support debt owed.

claims.quote: The State, or HHS if the State requests and HHS agrees, is required to provide a written notification to the debtor, pursuant to the provisions of 42 U.S.C. 664(a)(3) and 45 CFR 303.72(e), informing the debtor that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: The State, or HHS if requested, must provide a written notification to the debtor informing them of the intent to collect the debt through tax refund offset.

claims.quote: The notice also shall: (i) Instruct the debtor of the steps which may be taken to contest the State's determination that past-due support is owed or the amount of the past-due support; (ii) Advise any non-debtor who may file a joint tax return with the debtor of the steps which a non-debtor spouse may take in order to secure his or her proper share of the tax refund; and (iii) In cases when a debt is being enforced by more than one State, advise the debtor of his or her opportunities to request a review with the State enforcing collection or the State issuing the support order as prescribed by the provisions of 45 CFR 303.72(g).
claims.summary: The notice must instruct the debtor on contesting the debt, advise non-debtors on securing their share of the tax refund, and inform the debtor of opportunities for review if the debt is enforced by multiple states.

claims.quote: The State shall, in the manner and in the time frames provided by Fiscal Service or HHS, notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any deletion or net decrease in the amount of past-due support referred to Fiscal Service, or HHS as the case may be, for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: The State must notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any deletion or net decrease in the amount of past-due support referred for collection by tax refund offset.

claims.quote: When a State has knowledge that the debt is being enforced by more than one State, the State notifying Fiscal Service, or HHS as the case may be, of the debt shall inform any such other State involved in enforcing the debt when it receives the offset amount.
claims.summary: If a debt is being enforced by more than one State, the State notifying Fiscal Service or HHS must inform any other State involved in enforcing the debt when it receives the offset amount.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may reject a notification of past-due support which does not comply with the requirements of this section. Upon notification of the rejection and the reason for rejection, the State may resubmit a corrected notification.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may reject a notification of past-due support that does not comply with the requirements. The State may resubmit a corrected notification upon being notified of the rejection and the reason.

claims.quote: The State may notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any increases in the amount of the debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset provided that the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of this section with regard to those debts.
claims.summary: The State may notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any increases in the amount of the debt referred for collection by tax refund offset, provided the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (c)(4).

claims.quote: (2) Reduction of the tax refund payment pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 6402(a), (c), (d), and (e) shall occur prior to crediting the overpayment to any future liability for an internal revenue tax. Any amount remaining after tax refund offset under 26 U.S.C. 6402(a), (c), (d), and (e) shall be refunded to the taxpayer, or applied to estimated tax, if elected by the taxpayer pursuant to IRS regulations.
claims.summary: The reduction of the tax refund payment under 26 U.S.C. 6402(a), (c), (d), and (e) must occur before crediting the overpayment to any future liability for an internal revenue tax. Any remaining amount after the tax refund offset must be refunded to the taxpayer or applied to estimated tax if elected by the taxpayer under IRS regulations.

claims.quote: (e) Post-offset notice. (1)(i) Fiscal Service shall notify the debtor in writing of: (A) The amount and date of the offset to satisfy past-due support; (B) The State to which this amount has been paid or credited; and (C) A contact point within the State that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify the debtor in writing of the amount and date of the offset to satisfy past-due support, the State to which the amount has been paid or credited, and a contact point within the State that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.

claims.quote: (2) Fiscal Service will advise HHS of the names, mailing addresses, and identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due support were collected, of the amounts collected from each debtor through tax refund offset, the names of any non-debtor spouses who may have filed a joint return with the debtor, and of the State on whose behalf each collection was made. Alternatively, Fiscal Service will provide such information to each State that refers debts directly to Fiscal Service. Fiscal Service will inform HHS and each State that the payment source is a tax refund payment.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must advise HHS of the names, mailing addresses, and identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due support were collected, the amounts collected from each debtor through tax refund offset, the names of any non-debtor spouses who may have filed a joint return with the debtor, and the State on whose behalf each collection was made. Alternatively, Fiscal Service will provide such information to each State that refers debts directly to Fiscal Service. Fiscal Service must inform HHS and each State that the payment source is a tax refund payment.

claims.quote: (3) At least weekly, Fiscal Service will notify the IRS of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts owed for past-due support were collected from tax refund offsets and the amounts collected from each debtor.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify the IRS at least weekly of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts owed for past-due support were collected from tax refund offsets and the amounts collected from each debtor.

claims.quote: (4) At such time and in such manner as Fiscal Service and HHS agree, but no less than annually, Fiscal Service will advise HHS of the States which have furnished notices of past-due support, the number of cases in each State with respect to which such notices have been furnished, the amount of past-due support sought to be collected by each State, and the amount of such tax refund offset collections actually made in the case of each State. As Fiscal Service and HHS may agree, Fiscal Service may provide additional offset-related information about States which have furnished notices of past-due support.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must advise HHS at such time and in such manner as Fiscal Service and HHS agree, but no less than annually, of the States which have furnished notices of past-due support, the number of cases in each State with respect to which such notices have been furnished, the amount of past-due support sought to be collected by each State, and the amount of such tax refund offset collections actually made in the case of each State. Fiscal Service may provide additional offset-related information about States which have furnished notices of past-due support.

claims.quote: (g) Disposition of amounts collected. Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (i) of this section, to HHS or to the appropriate State. If IRS notifies Fiscal Service that a tax refund payment that was offset was erroneous or otherwise not due to the taxpayer, Fiscal Service will notify HHS or the appropriate State that the tax refund payment was not eligible for offset. Subject to paragraph (h) of this section, Fiscal Service may deduct the amount of the erroneous offset funds from amounts payable to HHS or the State, as the case may be; or, upon Fiscal Service's request, the State shall return promptly to the affected taxpayer or Fiscal Service an amount equal to the amount of the erroneous funds (unless the State previously has forwarded such amounts, or any portion of such amounts, to the affected taxpayer). HHS and States shall notify Fiscal Service any time HHS or a State returns an erroneous offset payment to an affected taxpayer. Fiscal Service and HHS, or the appropriate State, will adjust their debtor records accordingly.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (i) of this section, to HHS or to the appropriate State. If IRS notifies Fiscal Service that a tax refund payment that was offset was erroneous or otherwise not due to the taxpayer, Fiscal Service must notify HHS or the appropriate State that the tax refund payment was not eligible for offset. Subject to paragraph (h) of this section, Fiscal Service may deduct the amount of the erroneous offset funds from amounts payable to HHS or the State, as the case may be; or, upon Fiscal Service's request, the State shall return promptly to the affected taxpayer or Fiscal Service an amount equal to the amount of the erroneous funds (unless the State previously has forwarded such amounts, or any portion of such amounts, to the affected taxpayer). HHS and States must notify Fiscal Service any time HHS or a State returns an erroneous offset payment to an affected taxpayer. Fiscal Service and HHS, or the appropriate State, must adjust their debtor records accordingly.

claims.quote: (h) Time limitation. If IRS notifies Fiscal Service on or after January 1, 2016, that a tax refund payment that was offset was erroneous or otherwise not due to the taxpayer, Fiscal Service shall not deduct the amount of the erroneous offset funds from amounts due to HHS or the State, or otherwise demand return of the offset funds from the State pursuant to paragraph (g) of this section, if the date of IRS's notification to Fiscal Service in paragraph (g) is more than six months after the date the tax refund was offset ( i.e., the tax refund payment date); and the State has already forwarded the funds as required or authorized by 42 U.S.C. 657. This paragraph does not apply to paragraph (f) of this section.
claims.summary: If IRS notifies Fiscal Service on or after January 1, 2016, that a tax refund payment that was offset was erroneous or otherwise not due to the taxpayer, Fiscal Service shall not deduct the amount of the erroneous offset funds from amounts due to HHS or the State, or otherwise demand return of the offset funds from the State pursuant to paragraph (g) of this section, if the date of IRS's notification to Fiscal Service in paragraph (g) is more than six months after the date the tax refund was offset (i.e., the tax refund payment date); and the State has already forwarded the funds as required or authorized by 42 U.S.C. 657. This paragraph does not apply to paragraph (f) of this section.

claims.quote: (i) Fees. The State will pay a fee to Fiscal Service for the full cost of administering the tax refund offset program. The fee (not to exceed $25 per case submitted) will be established annually in such amount as Fiscal Service and HHS agree to be sufficient to reimburse Fiscal Service for the full cost of the offset procedure. Fiscal Service will deduct the fees from amounts collected prior to disposition and transmit a portion of the fees deducted to reimburse the IRS for its share of the cost of administering the tax refund offset program. Fees will be charged only for actual tax refund offsets completed.
claims.summary: The State must pay a fee to Fiscal Service for the full cost of administering the tax refund offset program. The fee (not to exceed $25 per case submitted) will be established annually in such amount as Fiscal Service and HHS agree to be sufficient to reimburse Fiscal Service for the full cost of the offset procedure. Fiscal Service must deduct the fees from amounts collected prior to disposition and transmit a portion of the fees deducted to reimburse the IRS for its share of the cost of administering the tax refund offset program. Fees will be charged only for actual tax refund offsets completed.

claims.quote: (j) Review of tax refund offsets. In accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(f), any reduction of a taxpayer's refund made pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), (d), or (e) shall not be subject to review by any court of the United States or by the Secretary of the Treasury, Fiscal Service or IRS in an administrative proceeding. No action brought against the United States to recover the amount of this reduction shall be considered to be a suit for refund of tax.
claims.summary: Any reduction of a taxpayer's refund made pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), (d), or (e) shall not be subject to review by any court of the United States or by the Secretary of the Treasury, Fiscal Service, or IRS in an administrative proceeding. No action brought against the United States to recover the amount of this reduction shall be considered to be a suit for refund of tax.

claims.quote: (k) Access to and use of confidential tax information. Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program is permitted to the extent necessary in establishing appropriate agency records, locating any person with respect to whom a reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(c) is sought for purposes of collecting the debt, and in the defense of any litigation or administrative procedure ensuing from a reduction made under section 6402(c).
claims.summary: Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program is permitted to the extent necessary in establishing appropriate agency records, locating any person with respect to whom a reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(c) is sought for purposes of collecting the debt, and in the defense of any litigation or administrative procedure ensuing from a reduction made under section 6402(c).

claims.quote: (m) Social Security numbers. Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail. In addition, Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer the tax refund offset program, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail. In addition, Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer the tax refund offset program, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall offset payments to satisfy, in whole or in part, debts owed by the payee.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must offset payments to satisfy debts owed by the payee.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall compare payment records with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must compare payment records with debt records submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: When a match occurs and all other requirements for offset have been met, the disbursing official shall offset the payment to satisfy, in whole or in part, the debt.
claims.summary: If a match occurs and all other requirements for offset are met, the disbursing official must offset the payment to satisfy the debt.

claims.quote: Covered benefit payments, i.e., payments made to individuals under the Social Security Act (other than Supplemental Security Income (SSI) payments), part B of the Black Lung Benefits Act, or any law administered by the Railroad Retirement Board (RRB) (other than tier 2 benefit payments) are among the types of payments which may be offset to collect debts owed to the United States.
claims.summary: Covered benefit payments may be offset to collect debts owed to the United States.

claims.quote: Offset of covered benefit payments are subject to the limitations contained in this section.
claims.summary: Offset of covered benefit payments is subject to the limitations in this section.

claims.quote: Offsets of covered benefit payments will occur only if the name and taxpayer identifying number of the person who is entitled to the benefit of all or a part of the payment matches the name and taxpayer identifying number of the debtor.
claims.summary: Offsets of covered benefit payments will occur only if the name and taxpayer identifying number of the person entitled to the benefit matches the debtor's name and taxpayer identifying number.

claims.quote: Creditor agencies must notify Fiscal Service of all past-due, legally enforceable debt delinquent for more than 120 days for purposes of collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must notify Fiscal Service of all past-due, legally enforceable debt delinquent for more than 120 days for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: Creditor agencies may notify Fiscal Service of all debt delinquent for less than 120 days for purposes of collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies may notify Fiscal Service of all debt delinquent for less than 120 days for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: Prior to such notification, creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the creditor agency has provided the debtor with notice and an opportunity for a review in accordance with the provisions of 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) and other applicable law.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the debtor has been provided notice and an opportunity for review.

claims.quote: The amount offset from a monthly covered benefit payment shall be the lesser of: (i) The amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties and administrative costs; (ii) An amount equal to 15% of the monthly covered benefit payment; or (iii) The amount, if any, by which the monthly covered benefit payment exceeds $750.
claims.summary: The amount offset from a monthly covered benefit payment must be the lesser of the debt amount, 15% of the monthly covered benefit payment, or the amount by which the monthly covered benefit payment exceeds $750.

claims.quote: A debtor shall not receive a refund of any amounts offset if the debtor's monthly covered benefit payments are reduced, suspended, terminated, or otherwise not received for a period of 12 months.
claims.summary: A debtor shall not receive a refund of any offset amounts if their monthly covered benefit payments are reduced, suspended, terminated, or not received for 12 months.

claims.quote: Before offsetting a covered benefit payment, the disbursing official will notify the payee in writing of the date offset will commence. The notice shall inform the payee of the type of payment that will be offset; the identity of the creditor agency which requested the offset; and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.summary: Before offsetting a covered benefit payment, the disbursing official must notify the payee in writing of the date offset will commence and provide details about the payment, creditor agency, and contact point.

claims.quote: The disbursing official conducting the offset will notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy, in whole or in part, a delinquent debt owed to the United States. The notice shall inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment that was offset; the identity of the creditor agency which requested the offset; and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.summary: The disbursing official conducting the offset must notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset and provide details about the payment, creditor agency, and contact point.

claims.quote: A fee which Fiscal Service has determined to be sufficient to cover the full cost of the offset procedure, shall be deducted from each offset amount.
claims.summary: A fee determined by Fiscal Service to cover the full cost of the offset procedure must be deducted from each offset amount.

claims.quote: The disbursing official conducting the offset will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (g) of this section, to the appropriate creditor agency.
claims.summary: The disbursing official conducting the offset must transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees, to the appropriate creditor agency.

claims.quote: If an erroneous offset payment is made to a creditor agency, the disbursing official will notify the creditor agency that an erroneous offset payment has been made.
claims.summary: If an erroneous offset payment is made to a creditor agency, the disbursing official must notify the creditor agency.

claims.quote: The disbursing official and the creditor agency shall adjust the debtor records appropriately.
claims.summary: The disbursing official and the creditor agency must adjust the debtor records appropriately.

document_title: 31 CFR Part 285 (point-in-time 2026-07-01)

category: Title 31 — Code of Federal Regulations parts

claims.quote: We offer securities under this part exclusively in book-entry form and as direct obligations of the United States issued under Chapter 31 of Title 31 of the United States Code.
claims.summary: The Treasury offers securities exclusively in book-entry form and as direct obligations of the United States.

claims.quote: When we issue additional securities with the same CUSIP number as outstanding securities, we consider them to be the same securities as the outstanding securities.
claims.summary: The Treasury considers additional securities with the same CUSIP number as outstanding securities to be the same securities.

claims.quote: Are issued at a discount or at par, depending upon the auction results;
claims.summary: Treasury bills are issued at a discount or at par, depending upon the auction results.

claims.quote: Are redeemed at their par amount at maturity;
claims.summary: Treasury bills are redeemed at their par amount at maturity.

claims.quote: Have maturities of not more than one year.
claims.summary: Treasury bills have maturities of not more than one year.

claims.quote: Are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the par amount;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the par amount.

claims.quote: Have interest payable semiannually;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes have interest payable semiannually.

claims.quote: Are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending upon the auction results;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending upon the auction results.

claims.quote: Have maturities of at least one year, but of not more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed 1 notes have maturities of at least one year, but of not more than ten years.

claims.quote: Are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the inflation-adjusted principal on each interest payment date;
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are issued with a stated rate of interest to be applied to the inflation-adjusted principal on each interest payment date.

claims.quote: Are redeemed at maturity at their inflation-adjusted principal, or at their par amount, whichever is greater;
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are redeemed at maturity at their inflation-adjusted principal, or at their par amount, whichever is greater.

claims.quote: Are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results (See appendix B for price and interest payment calculations and appendix C for Investment Considerations.)
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results.

claims.quote: Have maturities of at least one year, but not more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes have maturities of at least one year, but not more than ten years.

claims.quote: Are only reopened as scheduled or announced.
claims.summary: Treasury inflation-protected notes are only reopened as scheduled or announced.

claims.quote: Are issued with a stated spread to be added to the index rate for daily interest accrual throughout each interest payment period;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes are issued with a stated spread to be added to the index rate for daily interest accrual throughout each interest payment period.

claims.quote: Have a zero-percent minimum daily interest accrual rate;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes have a zero-percent minimum daily interest accrual rate.

claims.quote: Have interest payable quarterly;
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes have interest payable quarterly.

claims.quote: Are sold at discount, par, or premium depending on the auction results (See appendix B for price and interest payment calculations and appendix C for Investment Considerations.)
claims.summary: Treasury floating rate notes are sold at discount, par, or premium depending on the auction results.

claims.quote: Are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results;
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed bonds are sold at discount, par, or premium, depending on the auction results.

claims.quote: Have maturities of more than ten years.
claims.summary: Treasury non-indexed bonds have maturities of more than ten years.

claims.quote: All bids must be submitted using an approved method, which depends on the system into which the awarded securities will be issued.
claims.summary: Bidders must submit bids using an approved method based on the system for the awarded securities.

claims.quote: We must receive competitive and noncompetitive bids prior to their respective closing times, which are stated in the auction announcement. We will not include late bids in the auction.
claims.summary: Bidders must submit competitive and noncompetitive bids before their respective closing times as stated in the auction announcement; late bids will not be included.

claims.quote: You are bound by your bids after the closing time.
claims.summary: Bidders are bound by their bids after the closing time.

claims.quote: You must have an agreement on file with us under which you agree to our terms and conditions for access to our system for participating in our auctions.
claims.summary: Submitters must have an agreement on file with the Treasury agreeing to the terms and conditions for access to the system for participating in auctions.

claims.quote: You must submit your bids in accordance with the regulations governing the system in which the security will be held.
claims.summary: Bidders must submit bids in accordance with the regulations governing the system in which the security will be held.

claims.quote: All bids must state the par amount of securities bid for and must equal or exceed the minimum to bid amount stated in the auction announcement. Bids in larger amounts must be in the multiple stated in the auction announcement.
claims.summary: All bids must state the par amount of securities bid for and must equal or exceed the minimum to bid amount stated in the auction announcement. Bids in larger amounts must be in the multiple stated in the auction announcement.

claims.quote: You may not bid noncompetitively for more than $10 million. The maximum bid limitation does not apply if you are bidding solely through a request to reinvest the proceeds of a maturing security held directly with Treasury, which is a noncompetitive bid.
claims.summary: You may not bid noncompetitively for more than $10 million. The maximum bid limitation does not apply if you are bidding solely through a request to reinvest the proceeds of a maturing security held directly with Treasury, which is a noncompetitive bid.

claims.quote: You may not bid noncompetitively in an auction in which you are bidding competitively. You may not bid noncompetitively if, in the security being auctioned, you hold a position in when-issued trading or in futures or forward contracts at any time between the date of the auction announcement and the time we announce the auction results. During this same timeframe, a noncompetitive bidder may not enter into any agreement to purchase or sell or otherwise dispose of the securities it is acquiring in the auction.
claims.summary: You may not bid noncompetitively in an auction in which you are bidding competitively. You may not bid noncompetitively if, in the security being auctioned, you hold a position in when-issued trading or in futures or forward contracts at any time between the date of the auction announcement and the time we announce the auction results. During this same timeframe, a noncompetitive bidder may not enter into any agreement to purchase or sell or otherwise dispose of the securities it is acquiring in the auction.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the discount rate bid, expressed with three decimals in .005 increments. The third decimal must be either a zero or a five, for example, 5.320 or 5.325. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 5.32 will be treated as 5.320. The rate bid may be a positive number or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the discount rate bid, expressed with three decimals in .005 increments. The third decimal must be either a zero or a five, for example, 5.320 or 5.325. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 5.32 will be treated as 5.320. The rate bid may be a positive number or zero.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 4.170. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 4.1 will be treated as 4.100. The yield bid may be a positive number or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 4.170. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 4.1 will be treated as 4.100. The yield bid may be a positive number or zero.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the real yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 3.070. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 3 will be treated as 3.000. The real yield may be a positive number, a negative number, or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the real yield bid, expressed with three decimals, for example, 3.070. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 3 will be treated as 3.000. The real yield may be a positive number, a negative number, or zero.

claims.quote: A competitive bid must show the discount margin bid, expressed as a percentage with three decimals, for example, 0.290 percent. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 0.29 will be treated as 0.290. The discount margin bid may be positive, negative, or zero.
claims.summary: A competitive bid must show the discount margin bid, expressed as a percentage with three decimals, for example, 0.290 percent. We will treat any missing decimals as zero, for example, a bid of 0.29 will be treated as 0.290. The discount margin bid may be positive, negative, or zero.

claims.quote: There is no limit on the maximum dollar amount that you may bid for competitively, either at a single yield, discount rate, or discount margin, or at different yields, discount rates, or discount margins. However, a competitive bid at a single yield, discount rate, or discount margin that exceeds 35 percent of the offering amount will be reduced to that amount.
claims.summary: There is no limit on the maximum dollar amount that you may bid for competitively, either at a single yield, discount rate, or discount margin, or at different yields, discount rates, or discount margins. However, a competitive bid at a single yield, discount rate, or discount margin that exceeds 35 percent of the offering amount will be reduced to that amount.

claims.quote: You may not bid competitively in an auction in which you are bidding noncompetitively. You may not bid competitively for securities to be held directly with Treasury.
claims.summary: You may not bid competitively in an auction in which you are bidding noncompetitively. You may not bid competitively for securities to be held directly with Treasury.

claims.quote: If you are bidding competitively in an auction, you must report your net long position when the total of your bids plus your net long position in the security being auctioned equals or exceeds the net long position reporting threshold ( See table.).
claims.summary: You must report your net long position when the total of your bids plus your net long position in the security being auctioned equals or exceeds the net long position reporting threshold.

claims.quote: You must calculate your net long position as of one half-hour prior to the closing time for receipt of competitive bids.
claims.summary: You must calculate your net long position as of one half-hour prior to the closing time for receipt of competitive bids.

claims.quote: If you have more than one bid in an auction and you must report either your net long position or a zero, you must report that figure only once.
claims.summary: If you have more than one bid in an auction and you must report either your net long position or a zero, you must report that figure only once.

claims.quote: Finally, if you are a customer and must report either your net long position or a zero, you must report that figure through only one depository institution or dealer.
claims.summary: If you are a customer and must report either your net long position or a zero, you must report that figure through only one depository institution or dealer.

claims.quote: Only depository institutions or dealers may submit bids for customers ( see definitions at
claims.summary: Only depository institutions or dealers may submit bids for customers.

claims.quote: Submitters must remit payment for bids they submit on behalf of customers, including customers of intermediaries, that result in awards of securities in the auction.
claims.summary: Submitters must remit payment for bids they submit on behalf of customers that result in awards of securities in the auction.

claims.quote: Submitters must provide the names of customers whenever they submit bids for them.
claims.summary: Submitters must provide the names of customers whenever they submit bids for them.

claims.quote: For individuals, submitters must provide the customer's full name (first and last).
claims.summary: For individuals, submitters must provide the customer's full name (first and last).

claims.quote: For institutional customers, submitters must provide the name of the institution, and the bidder identification number if the customer provides it.
claims.summary: For institutional customers, submitters must provide the name of the institution, and the bidder identification number if the customer provides it.

claims.quote: For trusts or other fiduciary estates (See appendix A.), submitters must provide on the customer list: (1) The full name or title of the trustee or fiduciary; (2) A reference to the document creating the trust or fiduciary estate with date of execution; and (3) The employer identification number (not social security number) of the trust or fiduciary estate.
claims.summary: For trusts or other fiduciary estates, submitters must provide on the customer list: (1) The full name or title of the trustee or fiduciary; (2) A reference to the document creating the trust or fiduciary estate with date of execution; and (3) The employer identification number (not social security number) of the trust or fiduciary estate.

claims.quote: The submitter must inform a customer of the net long position reporting requirement (See § 356.13.) if the customer is bidding for $100 million or more of securities.
claims.summary: The submitter must inform a customer of the net long position reporting requirement if the customer is bidding for $100 million or more of securities.

claims.quote: If the submitter's or intermediary's personnel know that the customer's position information is not correct, the submitter or intermediary may not submit the customer's bid.
claims.summary: If the submitter's or intermediary's personnel know that the customer's position information is not correct, the submitter or intermediary may not submit the customer's bid.

claims.quote: For each noncompetitive bid, the submitter must provide the customer's name and the amount bid.
claims.summary: For each noncompetitive bid, the submitter must provide the customer's name and the amount bid.

claims.quote: If it provides a summary bid amount, the submitter must transmit the list of individual customers and their bid amounts by close of business on the auction day.
claims.summary: If it provides a summary bid amount, the submitter must transmit the list of individual customers and their bid amounts by close of business on the auction day.

claims.quote: However, the submitter must be able to provide the customer list details by the noncompetitive bidding deadline if requested.
claims.summary: The submitter must be able to provide the customer list details by the noncompetitive bidding deadline if requested.

claims.quote: If it is bidding competitively, an investment adviser must calculate the amount of its bids and positions for purposes of the net long position reporting requirement found in § 356.13(a).
claims.summary: An investment adviser must calculate the amount of its bids and positions for the net long position reporting requirement.

claims.quote: In addition to its own competitive bids and positions, the investment adviser must also include in the calculation all other competitive bids and positions that it controls.
claims.summary: An investment adviser must include all other competitive bids and positions it controls in the calculation for net long position reporting.

claims.quote: If the net long position is reportable, the investment adviser must report it as a total in connection with only one bid as stated in § 356.13(a).
claims.summary: An investment adviser must report the net long position as a total in connection with only one bid if it is reportable.

claims.quote: This requirement applies regardless of whether the investment adviser bids in its own name or in the name of its controlled accounts.
claims.summary: The net long position reporting requirement applies regardless of whether the investment adviser bids in its own name or in the name of its controlled accounts.

claims.quote: If an investment adviser does meet the reporting threshold, the table also shows which positions must be included in, and which may be excluded from, the net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include certain positions in the net long position calculation and may exclude others.

claims.quote: the investment adviser has a net long position for its own account that position must be included in the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include its own net long position in the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: the investment adviser's competitive bid is for a controlled account any net long position of that account must be included in the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include the net long position of a controlled account in the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: the controlled account has a net long position of $100 million or more that position must be included in the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must include the net long position of a controlled account of $100 million or more in the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: the controlled account has a net long position that is less than $100 million that position may be excluded from the investment adviser's net long position calculation.
claims.summary: The investment adviser may exclude the net long position of a controlled account less than $100 million from the net long position calculation.

claims.quote: any net long position is excluded under paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of this table all net short positions of controlled accounts under $100 million must also be excluded.
claims.summary: If a net long position is excluded, all net short positions of controlled accounts under $100 million must also be excluded.

claims.quote: When an investment adviser bids for a controlled account, we deem the investment adviser to have certified that it is complying with this part and the auction announcement for the security.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must certify compliance with this part and the auction announcement for the security.

claims.quote: we deem the investment adviser to have certified that the information it provided about bids for controlled accounts is accurate and complete.
claims.summary: The investment adviser must certify that the information provided about bids for controlled accounts is accurate and complete.

claims.quote: Investment advisers that submit competitive bids in the names of controlled accounts are responsible for prorating any awards at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin using the same percentage that we announce.
claims.summary: Investment advisers must prorate awards at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin using the same percentage announced.

claims.quote: You are in compliance with this part and the auction announcement;
claims.summary: Submitters must be in compliance with this part and the auction announcement.

claims.quote: The information provided with regard to any bids for your own account is accurate and complete;
claims.summary: Submitters must provide accurate and complete information regarding bids for their own account.

claims.quote: The information provided with regard to any bids for customers accurately and completely reflects information provided by your customers or intermediaries.
claims.summary: Submitters must ensure that information provided regarding bids for customers accurately reflects information provided by customers or intermediaries.

claims.quote: You are in compliance with this part and the applicable auction announcement;
claims.summary: Intermediaries must be in compliance with this part and the applicable auction announcement.

claims.quote: That the information you provided to a submitter or other intermediary with regard to bids for customers accurately and completely reflects information provided by those customers or intermediaries.
claims.summary: Intermediaries must ensure that the information provided to a submitter or other intermediary regarding bids for customers accurately reflects information provided by those customers or intermediaries.

claims.quote: You are in compliance with this part and the auction announcement and;
claims.summary: Customers must be in compliance with this part and the auction announcement.

claims.quote: The information you provided to the submitter or intermediary in connection with the bid is accurate and complete.
claims.summary: Customers must provide accurate and complete information to the submitter or intermediary in connection with the bid.

claims.quote: By bidding in an auction, you agree to pay the settlement amount for any securities awarded to you.
claims.summary: Bidders must agree to pay the settlement amount for any securities awarded to them.

claims.quote: You must pay for your awarded securities by a debit entry to a deposit account that you are authorized to debit or by using the redemption proceeds of your certificate of indebtedness.
claims.summary: Bidders must pay for awarded securities by a debit entry to a deposit account they are authorized to debit or by using redemption proceeds of their certificate of indebtedness.

claims.quote: payment of the settlement amount must be by charge to the funds account of a depository institution at a Federal Reserve Bank.
claims.summary: Payment of the settlement amount must be made by charging the funds account of a depository institution at a Federal Reserve Bank.

claims.quote: A submitter that does not have a funds account at a Federal Reserve Bank or that chooses not to pay by charge to its own funds account must have an approved autocharge agreement on file with us before submitting any bids.
claims.summary: A submitter without a funds account at a Federal Reserve Bank or choosing not to pay by charge to its own funds account must have an approved autocharge agreement on file with us before submitting any bids.

claims.quote: Any depository institution whose funds account will be charged under an autocharge agreement will receive advance notice from us of the total par amount of, and price to be charged for, securities awarded as a result of the submitter's bids.
claims.summary: Any depository institution whose funds account will be charged under an autocharge agreement will receive advance notice from us of the total par amount of, and price to be charged for, securities awarded as a result of the submitter's bids.

claims.quote: We must have acknowledged and have on file an autocharge agreement between the clearing corporation and a depository institution.
claims.summary: We must have acknowledged and have on file an autocharge agreement between the clearing corporation and a depository institution.

claims.quote: We must have acknowledged and have on file a delivery and payment agreement between the submitter and the clearing corporation.
claims.summary: We must have acknowledged and have on file a delivery and payment agreement between the submitter and the clearing corporation.

claims.quote: First we accept in full all non-competitive bids that were submitted by the noncompetitive bidding deadline. After the closing time for receipt of competitive bids we start accepting those at the lowest yields, discount rates, or discount margins, through successively higher yields, discount rates, or discount margins, up to the amount required to meet the offering amount.
claims.summary: The Treasury must accept non-competitive bids first and then competitive bids starting from the lowest yields, discount rates, or discount margins.

claims.quote: When necessary, we prorate bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin as described below. If the amount of noncompetitive bids would absorb all or most of the offering amount, we will accept competitive bids in an amount sufficient to provide a fair determination of the yield, discount rate, or discount margin for the securities we are auctioning.
claims.summary: The Treasury must prorate bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin if necessary and accept competitive bids to ensure a fair determination of the yield, discount rate, or discount margin.

claims.quote: We derive the percentage by dividing the remaining par amount needed to fill the offering amount by the par amount of the bids at the high yield, discount rate, or discount margin and rounding up to the next hundredth of a whole percentage point, for example, 17.13%.
claims.summary: The Treasury must calculate the percentage of bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin by dividing the remaining par amount needed to fill the offering amount by the par amount of the bids at the high yield, discount rate, or discount margin and rounding up to the next hundredth of a whole percentage point.

claims.quote: The interest rate we establish produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.
claims.summary: The Treasury must establish an interest rate that produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.

claims.quote: The interest rate we establish produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the weighted-average yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.
claims.summary: The Treasury must establish an interest rate that produces the price closest to, but not above, par when evaluated at the weighted-average yield of awards to successful competitive bidders.

claims.quote: The interest rate will be the spread plus the index rate (as it may be adjusted on the calendar day following each auction of 13-week bills) subject to a minimum daily interest accrual rate of zero percent.
claims.summary: The Treasury must set the interest rate for floating rate notes as the spread plus the index rate, subject to a minimum daily interest accrual rate of zero percent.

claims.quote: We round price calculations to six decimal places on the basis of price per hundred, for example, 99.954321 (See appendix B to this part).
claims.summary: The Treasury must round price calculations to six decimal places on the basis of price per hundred.

claims.quote: We award securities to both noncompetitive and competitive bidders at the price equivalent to the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which bids were accepted. For inflation-protected securities, the price for awarded securities is the price equivalent to the highest accepted real yield.
claims.summary: The Treasury must award securities to both noncompetitive and competitive bidders at the price equivalent to the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which bids were accepted. For inflation-protected securities, the price for awarded securities is the price equivalent to the highest accepted real yield.

claims.quote: We award securities to competitive bidders at the price equivalent to each yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which their bids were accepted.
claims.summary: The Treasury must award securities to competitive bidders at the price equivalent to each yield, discount rate, or discount margin at which their bids were accepted.

claims.quote: We award securities to noncompetitive bidders at the price equivalent to the weighted average yield, discount rate, or discount margin of accepted competitive bids.
claims.summary: The Treasury must award securities to noncompetitive bidders at the price equivalent to the weighted average yield, discount rate, or discount margin of accepted competitive bids.

claims.quote: We generally prorate bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin under § 356.20(a)(2) of this part.
claims.summary: Submitters must prorate bids at the highest accepted yield, discount rate, or discount margin under § 356.20(a)(2).

claims.quote: We always make awards for at least the minimum to bid, and above that amount we make awards in the appropriate multiple to bid.
claims.summary: Submitters must make awards for at least the minimum to bid and in appropriate multiples to bid.

claims.quote: Depository institutions and dealers, whether submitters or intermediaries, are responsible for prorating awards for their customers at the same percentage that we announce.
claims.summary: Depository institutions and dealers must prorate awards for their customers at the same percentage announced by the Treasury.

claims.quote: The maximum award to any noncompetitive bidder is $10 million.
claims.summary: Noncompetitive bidders must not receive an award exceeding $10 million.
