claims.quote: The maximum award is 35 percent of the offering amount less the bidder's net long position as reportable under § 356.13.
claims.summary: Competitive bidders must not receive an award exceeding 35 percent of the offering amount less their net long position as reportable under § 356.13.

claims.quote: We will use this combined amount for the purpose of this 35 percent award limit.
claims.summary: When bids and net long positions of multiple bidders must be combined, the combined amount must be used for the purpose of the 35 percent award limit.

claims.quote: After the conclusion of the auction, we will make the auction results available on our website at http://www.treasurydirect.gov.
claims.summary: The Treasury must make auction results available on its website at http://www.treasurydirect.gov after the auction concludes.

claims.quote: The auction results will include such information as: (1) The amounts of bids we accepted and the amount of securities we awarded; (2) The range of accepted yields, discount rates, or discount margins. (3) The proration percentage; (4) The interest rate for a note or bond; (5) A breakdown of the amounts of noncompetitive and competitive bids we accepted from, and awarded to, the public; (6) The amounts of bids tendered and accepted from the Federal Reserve Banks for their own accounts; (7) The bid-to-cover ratio; and (8) Other information that we may decide to include.
claims.summary: The Treasury must include specific information in auction results, such as accepted bids, securities awarded, accepted yields, proration percentage, interest rates, and bid-to-cover ratios.

claims.quote: We will provide notice to all submitters letting them know whether their bids were successful or not.
claims.summary: The agency must notify submitters whether their bids were successful or not.

claims.quote: If we are to deliver awarded securities under a delivery and payment agreement, we will provide notice of the awards to the clearing corporation that is a party to the agreement.
claims.summary: The agency must notify the clearing corporation of the awards if securities are to be delivered under a delivery and payment agreement.

claims.quote: If you are a submitter for customers, you are responsible for notifying them of their awards.
claims.summary: Submitters are responsible for notifying their customers of their awards.

claims.quote: You are also responsible for notifying any intermediaries that forwarded successful bids to you.
claims.summary: Submitters are responsible for notifying intermediaries that forwarded successful bids to them.

claims.quote: Similarly, an intermediary is responsible for providing notification of any awards to its customers and any intermedi, from whom it received bids.
claims.summary: Intermediaries are responsible for providing notification of awards to their customers and any intermediaries from whom they received bids.

claims.quote: We will provide notice to each depository institution that has entered into an autocharge agreement with a submitt, or a clearing corporation of the amount to be charged, on the issue date, to the institution's funds account at the Federal Reserve Bank servicing the institution.
claims.summary: The agency must notify depository institutions of the amount to be charged to their funds account at the Federal Reserve Bank.

claims.quote: We will provide this notification no later than the day after the auction.
claims.summary: The agency must provide notification to depository institutions no later than the day after the auction.

claims.quote: Any customer awarded a par amount of $2 billion or more in an auction must send us a confirmation in written form or via e-mail containing the information in paragraph (d)(1)(ii) of this section.
claims.summary: Customers awarded $2 billion or more must send a confirmation in written form or via e-mail.

claims.quote: The confirmation must be sent no later than 10 a.m. Eastern Time on the next business day following the auction.
claims.summary: Customers must send the confirmation no later than 10 a.m. Eastern Time on the next business day following the auction.

claims.quote: If sent in written form, the confirmation must be signed by the customer or authorized representative.
claims.summary: Written confirmations must be signed by the customer or authorized representative.

claims.quote: Confirmations sent by e-mail must be sent by the customer or authorized representative.
claims.summary: E-mail confirmations must be sent by the customer or authorized representative.

claims.quote: Confirmations signed or sent by an authorized representative must include the capacity in which the representative is acting.
claims.summary: Confirmations signed or sent by an authorized representative must include the representative's capacity.

claims.quote: The information the customer must provide is: (A) A confirmation of the awarded bid(s), including the name of each submitter that submitted the bid(s) on the customer's behalf, and (B) A statement indicating whether the customer had a reportable net long position as defined in § 356.13.
claims.summary: Customers must provide confirmation of awarded bids and a statement on whether they had a reportable net long position.

claims.quote: If a position had to be reported, the statement must provide the amount of the position and the name of the submitter that the customer requested to report the position.
claims.summary: If a position had to be reported, the statement must provide the amount of the position and the name of the submitter.

claims.quote: A submitter or intermediary submitting or forwarding bids for a customer must notify the customer of the customer confirmation reporting requirement if we award the customer $2 billion or more as a result of those bids.
claims.summary: Submitters or intermediaries must notify the customer of the confirmation reporting requirement if the customer is awarded $2 billion or more.

claims.quote: Securities bought in the auction must be paid for by the issue date.
claims.summary: Securities bought in the auction must be paid for by the issue date.

claims.quote: The payment amount for awarded securities will be the settlement amount as defined in § 356.2.
claims.summary: The payment amount for awarded securities is the settlement amount as defined in § 356.2.

claims.quote: If you are paying by debit entry to a deposit account as provided for in § 356.17(b), we will charge the settlement amount to the specified account on the issue date.
claims.summary: The agency must charge the settlement amount to the specified account on the issue date if payment is by debit entry to a deposit account.

claims.quote: Where the submitter's method of payment is an authorized charge to the funds account of a depository institution as provided for in § 356.17(c), we will charge the settlement amount to the specified funds account on the issue date.
claims.summary: The agency must charge the settlement amount to the specified funds account on the issue date if payment is by authorized charge to a depository institution's funds account.

claims.quote: we will redeem the certificate of indebtedness for the settlement amount of the security and apply the proceeds on the issue date.
claims.summary: The Treasury will redeem the certificate of indebtedness for the settlement amount of the security and apply the proceeds on the issue date.

claims.quote: we will pay principal on bills, notes, and bonds on the maturity date as specified in the auction announcement.
claims.summary: The Treasury will pay principal on bills, notes, and bonds on the maturity date as specified in the auction announcement.

claims.quote: Interest on notes and bonds accrues from the dated date. Interest is payable on a semiannual or quarterly basis on the interest payment dates specified in the auction announcement through the maturity date.
claims.summary: Interest on notes and bonds accrues from the dated date. Interest is payable on a semiannual or quarterly basis on the interest payment dates specified in the auction announcement through the maturity date.

claims.quote: If any principal or interest payment date is a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which the Federal Reserve System is not open for business, we will make the payment (without additional interest) on the next business day.
claims.summary: If any principal or interest payment date is a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which the Federal Reserve System is not open for business, the Treasury will make the payment (without additional interest) on the next business day.

claims.quote: If a bond is callable, we will pay the principal prior to maturity if we call it under its terms, which include providing appropriate public notice.
claims.summary: If a bond is callable, the Treasury will pay the principal prior to maturity if it calls the bond under its terms, which include providing appropriate public notice.

claims.quote: we will pay the inflation-adjusted principal.
claims.summary: The Treasury will pay the inflation-adjusted principal.

claims.quote: we will pay an additional amount so that the additional amount plus the inflation-adjusted principal equals the par amount.
claims.summary: The Treasury will pay an additional amount so that the additional amount plus the inflation-adjusted principal equals the par amount.

claims.quote: we will base the final interest payment on the inflation-adjusted principal at maturity.
claims.summary: The Treasury will base the final interest payment on the inflation-adjusted principal at maturity.

claims.quote: We discharge our payment obligations when we credit payment to the account maintained at a Federal Reserve Bank for a depository institution or other authorized entity, or when we make payment according to the instructions of the person or entity maintaining the account.
claims.summary: The Treasury will discharge its payment obligations when it credits payment to the account maintained at a Federal Reserve Bank for a depository institution or other authorized entity, or when it makes payment according to the instructions of the person or entity maintaining the account.

claims.quote: We also will not recognize the claims of any person or entity: (i) That does not have an account at a Federal Reserve Bank, or (ii) With respect to any accounts not maintained at a Federal Reserve Bank.
claims.summary: The Treasury will not recognize the claims of any person or entity that does not have an account at a Federal Reserve Bank, or with respect to any accounts not maintained at a Federal Reserve Bank.

claims.quote: We discharge our payment obligations when we make payment to a depository institution for credit to the account specified by the owner of the security, when we make payment for a certificate of indebtedness to be issued and held in the owner's account, or when we make payment according to the instructions of the security's owner or the owner's legal representative.
claims.summary: The Treasury will discharge its payment obligations when it makes payment to a depository institution for credit to the account specified by the owner of the security, when it makes payment for a certificate of indebtedness to be issued and held in the owner's account, or when it makes payment according to the instructions of the security's owner or the owner's legal representative.

claims.quote: These components must be maintained in the commercial book-entry system.
claims.summary: Components must be maintained in the commercial book-entry system.

claims.quote: The minimum par amount of a non-indexed security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.
claims.summary: The minimum par amount of a non-indexed security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.

claims.quote: Principal components stripped from non-indexed securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their par amount.
claims.summary: Principal components stripped from non-indexed securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their par amount.

claims.quote: Interest components stripped from non-indexed securities have the following features: (i) They are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their original payment value, which is derived by multiplying the semiannual interest rate and the par amount;
claims.summary: Interest components stripped from non-indexed securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their original payment value, which is derived by multiplying the semiannual interest rate and the par amount.

claims.quote: All interest components with the same maturity date have the same CUSIP number, regardless of the underlying security from which the interest payments were stripped, and therefore are fungible (interchangeable).
claims.summary: All interest components with the same maturity date have the same CUSIP number, regardless of the underlying security from which the interest payments were stripped, and therefore are fungible (interchangeable).

claims.quote: the CUSIP numbers of interest components are different from the CUSIP numbers of principal components and fully constituted securities, even if they have the same maturity date, and therefore are not fungible.
claims.summary: The CUSIP numbers of interest components are different from the CUSIP numbers of principal components and fully constituted securities, even if they have the same maturity date, and therefore are not fungible.

claims.quote: The minimum par amount of an inflation-protected security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.
claims.summary: The minimum par amount of an inflation-protected security that may be stripped is $100. Any par amount to be stripped above $100 must be in a multiple of $100.

claims.quote: At maturity, the holder will receive the inflation-adjusted principal or the par amount, whichever is greater.
claims.summary: At maturity, the holder will receive the inflation-adjusted principal or the par amount, whichever is greater.

claims.quote: Interest components stripped from inflation-protected securities are maintained in accounts, and transferred, at their adjusted value.
claims.summary: Interest components stripped from inflation-protected securities must be maintained and transferred at their adjusted value.

claims.quote: All interest components with the same maturity date have the same CUSIP number, regardless of the underlying security from which the interest payments were stripped.
claims.summary: All interest components with the same maturity date must have the same CUSIP number, regardless of the underlying security.

claims.quote: At maturity, the payment to the holder will be derived by multiplying the adjusted value of the interest component by the Reference CPI of the maturity date, divided by 100.
claims.summary: At maturity, the payment to the holder must be derived by multiplying the adjusted value of the interest component by the Reference CPI of the maturity date, divided by 100.

claims.quote: If the CPI is rebased to a different time base reference period... we will publish information that describes how this conversion will occur.
claims.summary: If the CPI is rebased to a different time base reference period, the agency must publish information describing how the conversion will occur.

claims.quote: A principal component and all related unmatured interest components, in the appropriate minimum or multiple amounts or adjusted values, must be submitted together for reconstitution.
claims.summary: A principal component and all related unmatured interest components must be submitted together for reconstitution in the appropriate minimum or multiple amounts or adjusted values.

claims.quote: Securities issued under this part are subject to all applicable taxes imposed under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or its successor.
claims.summary: Securities issued under this part are subject to all applicable taxes imposed under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or its successor.

claims.quote: Special federal income tax rules for inflation-protected securities, including stripped inflation-protected principal and interest components, are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.
claims.summary: Special federal income tax rules for inflation-protected securities, including stripped inflation-protected principal and interest components, are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.

claims.quote: Special federal income tax rules for floating rate notes are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.
claims.summary: Special federal income tax rules for floating rate notes are set forth in Internal Revenue Service regulations.

claims.quote: We have the discretion to: (1) Accept, reject, or refuse to recognize any bids submitted in an auction; (2) Award more or less than the amount of securities specified in the auction announcement; (3) Waive any provision of this part for any bidder or submitter; and (4) Change the terms and conditions of an auction.
claims.summary: The Treasury has discretion to accept, reject, or refuse bids, award varying amounts of securities, waive provisions, and change auction terms and conditions.

claims.quote: Our decisions under this part are final. We will provide a public notice if we change any auction provision, term, or condition.
claims.summary: The Treasury's decisions are final, and they must provide public notice if they change auction provisions, terms, or conditions.

claims.quote: We reserve the right to modify the terms and conditions of new securities and to depart from the customary pattern of securities offerings at any time.
claims.summary: The Treasury reserves the right to modify terms and conditions of new securities and depart from customary patterns of offerings.

claims.quote: If a person or entity fails to comply with any of the auction rules in this part, we will consider the circumstances and take what we deem to be appropriate action. This could include barring the person or entity from participating in future auctions under this part. We also may refer the matter to an appropriate regulatory agency.
claims.summary: A person or entity failing to comply with auction rules may be barred from future auctions and referred to a regulatory agency.

claims.quote: If you fail to pay for awarded securities in a timely manner, we may require you to pay liquidated damages of up to one percent of the par amount of securities we awarded to you. Our use of this liquidated damages remedy does not preclude us from using any other appropriate remedy.
claims.summary: Failure to pay for awarded securities in a timely manner may result in liquidated damages of up to one percent of the par amount of securities awarded.

document_title: 31 CFR Part 356 (point-in-time 2026-07-01)

category: Title 31 — Code of Federal Regulations parts

claims.quote: Any entity that meets the definition of an insurer under the Act is required to participate in the Program.
claims.summary: Entities meeting the definition of an insurer under the Act must participate in the Program.

claims.quote: (i) Premium information as reported to state regulators through the NAIC should be included in the calculation of direct earned premiums for purposes of the Program only to the extent it reflects premiums for property and casualty insurance issued by the insurer against losses occurring at the locations described in section 102(5)(A) and (B) of the Act.
claims.summary: Insurers must include premium information reported to state regulators through the NAIC in the calculation of direct earned premiums for the Program only to the extent it reflects premiums for property and casualty insurance against losses at specified locations.

claims.quote: (ii) Premiums for personal property and casualty lines of insurance (insurance primarily designed to cover personal, family or household risk exposures, with the exception of insurance written to insure 1 to 4 family rental dwellings owned for the business purpose of generating income for the property owner), or premiums for any other insurance coverage that does not meet the definition of property and casualty insurance, should be excluded in the calculation of direct earned premiums for purposes of the Program.
claims.summary: Premiums for personal property and casualty lines of insurance, or other coverage that does not meet the definition of property and casualty insurance, should be excluded in the calculation of direct earned premiums for the Program.

claims.quote: (iii) Personal property and casualty lines of insurance coverage that includes incidental coverage for commercial purposes are primarily personal coverage, and therefore premiums may be fully excluded by an insurer from the calculation of direct earned premium. For purposes of this section, commercial coverage is incidental if less than 25 percent of the total direct earned premium is attributable to commercial coverage.
claims.summary: Personal property and casualty lines of insurance with incidental commercial coverage may be fully excluded from direct earned premium calculations if less than 25% of the premium is attributable to commercial coverage.

claims.quote: (iv) If an insurance policy covers both commercial and personal property and casualty exposures, insurers may allocate the premiums in accordance with the proportion of risk between commercial and personal components in order to ascertain direct earned premium.
claims.summary: Insurers may allocate premiums based on the proportion of risk between commercial and personal components when calculating direct earned premium for policies covering both types of exposures.

claims.affected_party: insurers that do not report to NAIC
claims.quote: (i) Direct earned premium may be ascertained by adjusting data maintained by such insurer or reported by such insurer to its state regulator to reflect a breakdown of premiums for commercial and personal property and casualty exposure risk as described in paragraph (h)(1) of this section and, if necessary, re-stated to reflect the accrual method of determining direct earned premium versus direct premium.
claims.summary: Insurers not reporting to NAIC must adjust their data or reports to state regulators to reflect a breakdown of premiums for commercial and personal property and casualty exposure risk, and restate to the accrual method if necessary.

claims.affected_party: insurers that do not report to NAIC
claims.quote: (ii) Such an insurer should consider other types of payments that compensate the insurer for risk of loss (contributions, assessments, etc.) as part of its direct earned premium.
claims.summary: Insurers not reporting to NAIC should consider other payments compensating for risk of loss, such as contributions and assessments, as part of their direct earned premium.

claims.quote: (i) Direct written premium means the premium information for property and casualty insurance that is included by an insurer in column 1 of the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses of the NAIC Annual Statement or in an equivalent reporting requirement. The Federal terrorism policy surcharge is not included in amounts reported as direct written premium.
claims.summary: Direct written premium refers to the premium information included by insurers in column 1 of the NAIC Annual Statement or equivalent reporting requirements, excluding the Federal terrorism policy surcharge.

claims.quote: An insurer will be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements of the Act to the extent the insurer reasonably relied on Interim Guidance prior to the effective date of applicable regulations.
claims.summary: An insurer is deemed compliant with the Act if it reasonably relied on Interim Guidance before the effective date of applicable regulations.

claims.quote: An insurer or insurers must provide all relevant facts and circumstances concerning the relationship(s) between or among the affected insurers and the control factors in § 50.4(c)(4)(i) through (iv); and must explain in detail any basis for why the insurer believes that no controlling influence exists (if a presumption is being rebutted) in light of the particular facts and circumstances, as well as the Act's language, structure and purpose.
claims.summary: An insurer must provide all relevant facts and circumstances regarding relationships and control factors, and explain why no controlling influence exists if rebutting a presumption.

claims.quote: Unless otherwise extended by Treasury, within 60 days after receipt of a complete submission, including any additional information requested by Treasury, and including any oral presentation, Treasury will issue a final determination of whether one insurer has a controlling influence over another insurer for purposes of the Program.
claims.summary: Treasury will issue a final determination within 60 days after receiving a complete submission, including any additional information requested.

claims.affected_party: Persons actually or potentially affected by the Act or regulations in this Part
claims.quote: Persons actually or potentially affected by the Act or regulations in this Part may request an interpretation of the Act or regulations by writing to the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Office, Room 1410, Department of the Treasury, 1500 Pennsylvania Ave. NW., Washington, DC 20220, giving a detailed explanation of the facts and circumstances and the reason why an interpretation is needed.
claims.summary: Persons affected by the Act or regulations may request an interpretation by writing to the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Office with detailed explanations.

claims.quote: A requester should segregate and mark any confidential business or trade secret information clearly.
claims.summary: Requesters must segregate and mark any confidential business or trade secret information clearly.

claims.quote: The disclosure required by the Act must be made on a separate line item in the policy, at the time of offer and of renewal of the policy.
claims.summary: The disclosure required by the Act must be made on a separate line item in the policy at the time of offer and renewal.

claims.quote: An insurer may describe the premium charged for insured losses covered by the Program as a portion or percentage of a policy premium, if consistent with standard business practice and provided that the amount of policy premium or the method of determining the policy premium is also stated.
claims.summary: An insurer may describe the premium as a portion or percentage of a policy premium, provided that the amount or method of determining the policy premium is also stated.

claims.quote: An insurer may not describe the premium in a manner that is misleading in the context of the Program, such as by characterizing the premium as a "surcharge."
claims.summary: An insurer may not describe the premium in a misleading manner, such as by characterizing it as a "surcharge."

claims.quote: Subject to § 50.10(b), an insurer may provide disclosures using normal business practices, including forms and methods of communication used to communicate similar policyholder information to policyholders.
claims.summary: An insurer may provide disclosures using normal business practices, including forms and methods of communication used for similar policyholder information.

claims.quote: If an insurer normally communicates with a policyholder through an insurance producer or other intermediary, an insurer may provide disclosures through such producer or other intermediary. If an insurer elects to make the disclosures through an insurance producer or other intermediary, the insurer remains responsible for ensuring that the disclosures are provided by the insurance producer or other intermediary to policyholders in accordance with the Act.
claims.summary: An insurer may provide disclosures through an insurance producer or intermediary, but remains responsible for ensuring that the disclosures are provided to policyholders in accordance with the Act.

claims.quote: An insurer may demonstrate that it has satisfied the requirement to provide clear and conspicuous disclosure as described in
claims.summary: An insurer may demonstrate that it has satisfied the requirement to provide clear and conspicuous disclosure as described in the regulations.

claims.quote: An insurer must certify that it has complied with the requirement to provide disclosure to the policyholder on all policies that form the basis for any claim that is submitted by an insurer for Federal payment under the Program.
claims.summary: An insurer must certify compliance with the requirement to provide disclosure to the policyholder on all policies that form the basis for any claim submitted for Federal payment under the Program.

claims.quote: An insurer is deemed to be in compliance with the requirement of providing disclosure "at the time of offer and of renewal of the policy" under § 50.10(b) if the insurer makes the disclosure no later than the time the insurer first formally offers to provide insurance coverage or renew a policy for a current policyholder.
claims.summary: An insurer is deemed in compliance with the requirement to provide disclosure at the time of offer and renewal of the policy if the disclosure is made no later than the time the insurer first formally offers to provide insurance coverage or renews a policy for a current policyholder.

claims.quote: An insurer is deemed to be in compliance with the requirement of providing disclosure on a "separate line item in the policy" under § 50.10(b) if the insurer makes the disclosure: (a) On the declarations page of the policy; (b) Elsewhere within the policy itself; or (c) In any rider or endorsement, or other document that is made a part of the policy.
claims.summary: An insurer is deemed in compliance with the requirement to provide disclosure on a separate line item in the policy if the disclosure is made on the declarations page of the policy, elsewhere within the policy itself, or in any rider or endorsement, or other document that is made a part of the policy.

claims.quote: As a condition for Federal payments under section 103(b) of the Act, an insurer must provide clear and conspicuous disclosure to the policyholder of the existence of the $100,000,000,000 cap under section 103(e)(2). The cap disclosure must be made at the time of offer, purchase, and renewal of the policy.
claims.summary: As a condition for Federal payments under section 103(b) of the Act, an insurer must provide clear and conspicuous disclosure to the policyholder of the existence of the $100,000,000,000 cap under section 103(e)(2). The cap disclosure must be made at the time of offer, purchase, and renewal of the policy.

claims.quote: An insurer is deemed to be in compliance with the requirement of providing disclosure "at the time of offer, purchase, and renewal of the policy" under § 50.15(b) if the insurer: (1) Makes the disclosure no later than the time the insurer first formally offers to provide insurance coverage or renew a policy for a current policyholder; and (2) If terrorism risk coverage is purchased, the insurer makes clear and conspicuous reference back to that disclosure, as well as the final terms of terrorism insurance coverage, at the time the transaction is completed.
claims.summary: An insurer is deemed in compliance with the requirement to provide disclosure at the time of offer, purchase, and renewal of the policy under § 50.15(b) if the insurer makes the disclosure no later than the time the insurer first formally offers to provide insurance coverage or renews a policy for a current policyholder, and if terrorism risk coverage is purchased, makes clear and conspicuous reference back to that disclosure, as well as the final terms of terrorism insurance coverage, at the time the transaction is completed.

claims.quote: § 50.15(b) is deemed to be in compliance with the disclosure requirements if the insurer uses NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 1 or NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 2, as appropriate.
claims.summary: An insurer is deemed to be in compliance with the disclosure requirements if it uses NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 1 or NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 2, as appropriate.

claims.quote: An insurer is not required to use NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 1 or NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 2 to satisfy the disclosure requirements.
claims.summary: An insurer is not required to use NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 1 or NAIC Model Disclosure Form No. 2 to satisfy the disclosure requirements.

claims.quote: An insurer may use other means to comply with the disclosure requirements, as long as the disclosures comport with the requirements of the Act.
claims.summary: An insurer may use other means to comply with the disclosure requirements, as long as the disclosures comport with the requirements of the Act.

claims.quote: Under section 103(c) of the Act, an insurer must: (1) Make available, in all of its property and casualty insurance policies, coverage for insured losses; and (2) Make available property and casualty insurance coverage for insured losses that does not differ materially from the terms, amounts, and other coverage limitations applicable to losses arising from events other than acts of terrorism.
claims.summary: Under section 103(c) of the Act, an insurer must make available, in all of its property and casualty insurance policies, coverage for insured losses, and make available property and casualty insurance coverage for insured losses that does not differ materially from the terms, amounts, and other coverage limitations applicable to losses arising from events other than acts of terrorism.

claims.quote: Under section 108(a) of the Act, an insurer must comply with paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section through calendar year 2027.
claims.summary: Under section 108(a) of the Act, an insurer must comply with paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) of this section through calendar year 2027.

claims.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph (a)(2) of this section and § 50.21, property and casualty insurance coverage for insured losses does not have to be made available beyond December 31, 2027, even if the policy period of insurance coverage for losses from events other than acts of terrorism extends beyond that date.
claims.summary: Property and casualty insurance coverage for insured losses does not have to be made available beyond December 31, 2027, even if the policy period of insurance coverage for losses from events other than acts of terrorism extends beyond that date.

claims.quote: The requirement to make available coverage as provided in § 50.20 applies at the time an insurer makes the initial offer of coverage as well as at the time an insurer makes an initial offer of renewal of an existing policy.
claims.summary: The requirement to make available coverage as provided in § 50.20 applies at the time an insurer makes the initial offer of coverage as well as at the time an insurer makes an initial offer of renewal of an existing policy.

claims.quote: An insurer must make available coverage for insured losses in a policy of property and casualty insurance consistent with the definition of an act of terrorism as defined in
claims.summary: An insurer must make available coverage for insured losses in a policy of property and casualty insurance consistent with the definition of an act of terrorism as defined in

claims.affected_party: State residual market insurance entities and State workers' compensation funds
claims.quote: State residual market insurance entities and State workers' compensation funds are mandatory participants in the Program subject to the rules issued in this Subpart.
claims.summary: State residual market insurance entities and State workers' compensation funds must participate in the Program.

claims.affected_party: State residual market insurance entities and state workers' compensation funds deemed to be separate insurers
claims.quote: A state residual market insurance entity or a state workers' compensation fund that is deemed to be a separate insurer should follow the guidelines specified in § 50.4(h)(1) or (2) for the purposes of calculating the appropriate measure of direct earned premium.
claims.summary: These entities must follow the guidelines in § 50.4(h)(1) or (2) for calculating direct earned premium.

claims.affected_party: State residual market insurance entities and State workers' compensation funds deemed not to be separate insurers
claims.quote: A state residual market insurance entity or a State workers' compensation fund that is deemed not to be a separate insurer should continue to report, in accordance with normal business practices, to each participant insurer its share of premium income and insured losses, which shall then be included respectively in the participant insurer's direct earned premium or insured loss calculations.
claims.summary: These entities must report their share of premium income and insured losses to participant insurers.

claims.quote: Premium income that is distributed to or assumed by participant insurers in a state residual market insurance entity or state workers' compensation fund (whether directly or as quota share insurers of risks written by servicing carriers), shall be included in direct earned premium (as described in § 50.4(h)(1) or (2)) of the participant insurer.
claims.summary: Participant insurers must include distributed premium income in their direct earned premium calculations.

claims.quote: Treasury may request from insurers such data and information as may be reasonably required in support of Treasury's administration of the Program.
claims.summary: Insurers must provide data and information as reasonably required by Treasury for the administration of the Program.

claims.quote: No later than May 15 of each calendar year, all insurers shall provide specified data and information respecting their Program participation.
claims.summary: Insurers must provide specified data and information respecting their Program participation no later than May 15 of each calendar year.

claims.quote: Each insurer shall submit the required data and information by electronic submission through the forms and data portal(s) identified on Treasury's Web site.
claims.summary: Each insurer must submit the required data and information by electronic submission through the forms and data portal(s) identified on Treasury's Web site.

claims.quote: All data and information provided as part of such electronic submission shall be certified by the insurer as a full and true statement of the information provided to the best of its knowledge, information and belief.
claims.summary: All data and information provided as part of such electronic submission shall be certified by the insurer as a full and true statement of the information provided to the best of its knowledge, information and belief.

claims.quote: Insurers shall respond to any such supplemental requests as may be made within the timeframe and in the manner specified by Treasury.
claims.summary: Insurers shall respond to any such supplemental requests as may be made within the timeframe and in the manner specified by Treasury.

claims.quote: The Secretary may collect information relating to small insurers, as defined in § 50.4(z), in order to conduct a study of small insurers participating in the Program, and identify any competitive challenges small insurers face in the terrorism risk insurance marketplace.
claims.summary: The Secretary may collect information relating to small insurers, as defined in § 50.4(z), in order to conduct a study of small insurers participating in the Program, and identify any competitive challenges small insurers face in the terrorism risk insurance marketplace.

claims.quote: Information collected concerning small insurers may include information necessary for Treasury to identify: (1) Changes to the market share, premium volume, and policyholder surplus of small insurers relative to large insurers; (2) How the property and casualty insurance market for terrorism risk differs between small and large insurers, and whether such a difference exists within other perils; (3) The impact on small insurers of the Program's mandatory availability requirement under section 103(c) of the Act; (4) The effect on small insurers of increasing the trigger amount for the Program under section 103(e)(1)(B) of the Act; (5) The availability and cost of private reinsurance for small insurers; and (6) The impact that state workers compensation laws have on small insurers and workers compensation carriers in the terrorism risk insurance marketplace.
claims.summary: Information collected concerning small insurers may include information necessary for Treasury to identify: (1) Changes to the market share, premium volume, and policyholder surplus of small insurers relative to large insurers; (2) How the property and casualty insurance market for terrorism risk differs between small and large insurers, and whether such a difference exists within other perils; (3) The impact on small insurers of the Program's mandatory availability requirement under section 103(c) of the Act; (4) The effect on small insurers of increasing the trigger amount for the Program under section 103(e)(1)(B) of the Act; (5) The availability and cost of private reinsurance for small insurers; and (6) The impact that state workers compensation laws have on small insurers and workers compensation carriers in the terrorism risk insurance marketplace.

claims.quote: Subsequent to any certification by the Secretary of an act of terrorism, insurers shall report to Treasury information respecting insured losses arising from the act of terrorism.
claims.summary: Insurers must report to Treasury information about insured losses arising from an act of terrorism after certification.

claims.quote: Reporting under this subsection shall be by a form prescribed by Treasury and made available on the Treasury Web site, which provides basic information about each claim established by an insurer that involves or potentially involves an insured loss.
claims.summary: Insurers must report using a form prescribed by Treasury and made available on the Treasury Web site.

claims.quote: Information to be reported for any claims by or against a policyholder shall identify paid and reserved amounts associated with the claim.
claims.summary: Insurers must report paid and reserved amounts associated with claims.

claims.quote: In the case of an affiliated group of insurers, the form required by this subsection shall be submitted by a single insurer designated within the affiliated group, which shall report on a consolidated basis.
claims.summary: An affiliated group of insurers must submit a single report on a consolidated basis.

claims.quote: Data and information reported under this subsection will include: (1) A listing of each claim by name of insured, catastrophe code, line of business, and in the case of an affiliated group of insurers, the particular insurer or insurers within the group associated with each claim;
claims.summary: Insurers must include a listing of each claim with specific details such as name of insured, catastrophe code, line of business, and associated insurers in the case of an affiliated group.

claims.quote: (2) Amounts paid, both loss and loss adjustment expenses, in connection with the claim as of the effective date of the report; and (3) Amounts reserved, both loss and loss adjustment expenses, in connection with the claim as of the effective date of the report.
claims.summary: Insurers must report amounts paid and reserved, both loss and loss adjustment expenses, as of the effective date of the report.

claims.quote: To the extent that an insurer has established one or more claims that it believes involve insured losses arising from an act of terrorism, the insurer shall submit its first report within 60 days of establishing the first of such claims. An updated report shall be submitted each month thereafter, reporting data as of the prior month, until all claims arising from the act of terrorism have been resolved.
claims.summary: Insurers must submit their first report within 60 days of establishing a claim involving insured losses from an act of terrorism and submit updated reports monthly until all such claims are resolved.

claims.quote: An insurer subject to such a data call shall respond to this request within the time frame specified in the request.
claims.summary: Insurers must respond to data requests from Treasury within the time frame specified in the request.

claims.quote: All nonpublic information submitted to the Secretary under subparts F and G of this part shall be considered proprietary information and shall: (1) Be handled and stored by Treasury in an appropriately secure manner;
claims.summary: Treasury must handle and store nonpublic information in an appropriately secure manner.

claims.quote: All nonpublic information submitted to the Secretary under subparts F and G of this part shall be considered proprietary information and shall: (2) Be considered, where appropriate, to be trade secrets or commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential;
claims.summary: Treasury must consider nonpublic information as trade secrets or commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential.

claims.quote: All nonpublic information submitted to the Secretary under subparts F and G of this part shall be considered proprietary information and shall: (3) Not be publicly released in any unaggregated form in which a consumer, policyholder, or insurer is identifiable.
claims.summary: Treasury must not publicly release nonpublic information in any unaggregated form in which a consumer, policyholder, or insurer is identifiable.

claims.quote: Such insurance statistical aggregator shall keep any nonpublic information that it collects confidential, consistent with the requirements of this section.
claims.summary: Insurance statistical aggregators must keep nonpublic information confidential, consistent with the requirements of this section.

claims.affected_party: Secretary, state insurance regulatory authorities, other entities
claims.quote: The submission of any non-publicly available data and information to the Secretary under subparts F and G of this part, and the sharing of any non-publicly available data with or by the Secretary among other Federal agencies, the state insurance regulatory authorities, or any other entities shall not constitute a waiver of, or otherwise affect, any privilege or immunity arising under Federal or state law (including the rules of any Federal or state court) to which the data or information is otherwise subject.
claims.summary: The submission or sharing of non-publicly available data and information to the Secretary shall not constitute a waiver of, or otherwise affect, any privilege or immunity arising under Federal or state law.

claims.quote: Any requirement under Federal or state law to the extent otherwise applicable, or any requirement pursuant to a written agreement in effect between the original source of any non-publicly available data or information and the source of such data or information to the Secretary, regarding privacy or confidentiality of any data or information in the possession of the source to the Secretary, shall continue to apply to such data or information after the data or information has been provided pursuant to this subpart.
claims.summary: Requirements under Federal or state law or written agreements regarding privacy or confidentiality of data or information in the possession of the source to the Secretary shall continue to apply after the data or information has been provided pursuant to this subpart.

claims.quote: Any data or information obtained by the Secretary under subparts F or G of this part may be made available to state insurance regulatory authorities, individually or collectively through an information-sharing agreement that: (i) Shall comply with applicable Federal law; and (ii) Shall not constitute a waiver of, or otherwise affect, any privilege or immunity under Federal or state law (including any privilege referred to in paragraph (b)(1) of this section and the rules of any Federal or State court) to which the data or information is otherwise subject.
claims.summary: Data or information obtained by the Secretary under subparts F or G may be made available to state insurance regulatory authorities through an information-sharing agreement that complies with applicable Federal law and does not constitute a waiver of, or otherwise affect, any privilege or immunity under Federal or state law.

claims.quote: Section 552 of title 5, United States Code, including any exceptions thereunder, shall apply to any data or information submitted under this Subpart by an insurer or affiliate of an insurer.
claims.summary: Section 552 of title 5, United States Code, including any exceptions thereunder, shall apply to any data or information submitted under this Subpart by an insurer or affiliate of an insurer.

claims.quote: The Secretary, in consultation with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security, is responsible for determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.
claims.summary: The Secretary, in consultation with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security, is responsible for determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: The Secretary's review finds that the act satisfies the elements for certification under § 50.4(b)(1)(i) through (iv), and that it is not otherwise precluded from certification by
claims.summary: The Secretary's review must find that the act satisfies the elements for certification under § 50.4(b)(1)(i) through (iv), and that it is not otherwise precluded from certification by

claims.effective_date: 30 days or as soon as otherwise practicable after the review concludes
claims.quote: Within 30 days or as soon as otherwise practicable after the review identified in paragraph (b)(3) of this section concludes that the act satisfies the necessary criteria, the Secretary consults with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security pursuant to section 102(1)(A) of the Act.
claims.summary: The Secretary must consult with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security within 30 days or as soon as otherwise practicable after the review concludes that the act satisfies the necessary criteria.

claims.effective_date: 30 days of the Secretary commencing review
claims.quote: Treasury shall publish a notice in the Federal Register within 30 days of the Secretary commencing review notifying the public that the act is under review for certification as an act of terrorism.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a notice in the Federal Register within 30 days of the Secretary commencing review notifying the public that the act is under review for certification as an act of terrorism.

claims.effective_date: Not later than 30 days following the publication of a notice under paragraph (a) of this section that an act is under review for certification, and not later than every 60 days thereafter until the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism
claims.quote: Not later than 30 days following the publication of a notice under paragraph (a) of this section that an act is under review for certification, and not later than every 60 days thereafter until the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall publish a notice in the Federal Register notifying the public whether the act is still under review for certification as an act of terrorism.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a notice in the Federal Register not later than 30 days following the publication of a notice under paragraph (a) of this section that an act is under review for certification, and not later than every 60 days thereafter until the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, notifying the public whether the act is still under review for certification as an act of terrorism.

claims.effective_date: If circumstances relating to an act render timely notification under this section by Treasury impracticable
claims.quote: If, in the discretion of the Secretary, circumstances relating to an act render timely notification under this section by Treasury impracticable, Treasury shall provide the notification as soon as practicable, in a manner the Secretary determines is appropriate.
claims.summary: If circumstances relating to an act render timely notification under this section by Treasury impracticable, Treasury shall provide the notification as soon as practicable, in a manner the Secretary determines is appropriate.

claims.quote: The information sought by the Secretary shall be specified in the data request, and any insurer subject to the data request shall respond to the request within the time frame specified by the Secretary at the time of the request.
claims.summary: An insurer subject to a data request must respond to the request within the time frame specified by the Secretary.

claims.quote: Not later than 5 business days after the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall publish a statement and submit a notice to the Federal Register notifying the public of the Secretary's decision.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a statement and submit a notice to the Federal Register within 5 business days of determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Not later than 5 business days after the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall notify in writing any relevant supervisory officials of the Secretary's decision.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify relevant supervisory officials in writing within 5 business days of determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Not later than 5 business days after the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall notify in writing the President of the U.S. Senate and the Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives of the Secretary's decision.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify the President of the U.S. Senate and the Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives in writing within 5 business days of determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: The Secretary may request information with respect to loss estimates and likely affected insurers from organizations, including state insurance regulators, insurance modeling organizations, rating agencies, insurance brokers and producers, and insurance data aggregators.
claims.summary: The Secretary may request information from organizations such as state insurance regulators, insurance modeling organizations, rating agencies, insurance brokers and producers, and insurance data aggregators.

claims.quote: The Secretary, when evaluating an act for certification as an act of terrorism, may at any time direct one or more insurers to submit information regarding projected and actual losses in connection with an act and any other information the Secretary determines appropriate.
claims.summary: The Secretary may direct insurers to submit information regarding projected and actual losses in connection with an act and any other information the Secretary determines appropriate.

claims.quote: The data requested may include actual loss reserves established by insurers in connection with the act under consideration, loss estimates generated by insurers in connection with the act under consideration which have not yet been established as actual loss reserves, and information respecting an insurer's property and casualty exposures in a particular geographic area associated with the act under consideration.
claims.summary: The data requested may include actual loss reserves, loss estimates, and information respecting an insurer's property and casualty exposures in a particular geographic area associated with the act under consideration.

claims.quote: The percentages in paragraph (a)(1) of this section are subject to any adjustments described in
claims.summary: The percentages in paragraph (a)(1) of this section are subject to any adjustments described in the document.

claims.quote: Federal compensation will not be paid by Treasury unless the aggregate industry insured losses resulting from one or more certified acts of terrorism exceed the following amounts:
claims.summary: Federal compensation will not be paid unless aggregate industry insured losses from certified acts of terrorism exceed specified amounts.

claims.quote: Treasury shall pay the appropriate amount of the Federal share of compensation for an insured loss to an insurer upon a determination that:
claims.summary: Treasury must pay the Federal share of compensation for an insured loss upon determination that certain conditions are met.

claims.quote: The insurer has provided a clear and conspicuous disclosure as required by §§ 50.10 through 50,14 and a cap disclosure as required by § 50.15;
claims.summary: The insurer must provide clear and conspicuous disclosure as required by §§ 50.10 through 50.14 and a cap disclosure as required by § 50.15.

claims.quote: The insurer offered coverage for insured losses and the offer was accepted by the insured prior to the act which results in the insured loss;
claims.summary: The insurer must have offered coverage for insured losses and the offer must have been accepted by the insured prior to the act resulting in the insured loss.

claims.quote: The insurer took all steps reasonably necessary to properly and carefully investigate the insured loss and otherwise processed the insured loss using practices appropriate for the business of insurance;
claims.summary: The insurer must take all steps reasonably necessary to properly and carefully investigate the insured loss and process it using practices appropriate for the business of insurance.

claims.quote: The insured loss is within the scope of coverage issued by the insurer under the terms and conditions of one or more policies for commercial property and casualty insurance as defined in § 50.4(w);
claims.summary: The insured loss must be within the scope of coverage issued by the insurer under the terms and conditions of one or more policies for commercial property and casualty insurance as defined in § 50.4(w).

claims.quote: The procedures specified in this Subpart have been followed and all conditions for payment have been met.
claims.summary: The insurer must have followed the procedures specified in this Subpart and met all conditions for payment.

claims.quote: Treasury may subsequently adjust, including requiring repayment of, any payment made under paragraph (c) of this section in accordance with its authority under the Act.
claims.summary: Treasury may adjust or require repayment of any payment made under paragraph (c) of this section in accordance with its authority under the Act.

claims.quote: Upon a determination by Treasury that an insurer has failed to meet any of the requirements for payment specified in paragraph (c) of this section for a particular insured loss, Treasury may suspend payment of the Federal share of compensation for all other insured losses of the insurer pending investigation and audit of the insurer's insured losses.
claims.summary: Treasury may suspend payment of the Federal share of compensation for all other insured losses of an insurer if it determines the insurer has failed to meet any of the requirements for payment specified in paragraph (c) of this section.

claims.quote: Treasury will determine the amount of aggregate industry insured losses resulting from a certified act of terrorism. If aggregate industry insured losses in a calendar year resulting from one or more certified acts of terrorism exceed the applicable Program Trigger amounts specified in paragraph (b) of this section, Treasury will publish a document in the Federal Register of a Program Trigger Event.
claims.summary: Treasury must determine the amount of aggregate industry insured losses resulting from a certified act of terrorism and publish a document in the Federal Register of a Program Trigger Event if the losses exceed the applicable Program Trigger amounts.

claims.quote: The aggregate amount of insured losses of an insurer in a calendar year used to calculate the Federal share of compensation shall be reduced by any amounts recovered by the insurer as salvage or subrogation for its insured losses in the calendar year.
claims.summary: The insurer must reduce the aggregate amount of insured losses by any amounts recovered as salvage or subrogation for its insured losses in the calendar year.

claims.quote: The sum of the Federal share of compensation paid by Treasury to an insurer and the insurer's recoveries for insured losses from other sources shall not be greater than the insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism in that calendar year.
claims.summary: The sum of the Federal share of compensation paid by Treasury to an insurer and the insurer's recoveries for insured losses from other sources shall not exceed the insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism in that calendar year.

claims.quote: Amounts recovered for insured losses in excess of an insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism in a calendar year shall be repaid to Treasury within 45 days after the end of the month in which total recoveries of the insurer, from all sources, become excess.
claims.summary: Amounts recovered for insured losses in excess of an insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism in a calendar year shall be repaid to Treasury within 45 days after the end of the month in which total recoveries of the insurer, from all sources, become excess.

claims.quote: The Federal share of compensation for insured losses under the Program shall be reduced by the amount of other compensation provided by other Federal programs to an insured or a third party to the extent such other compensation duplicates the insurance indemnification for those insured losses.
claims.summary: The Federal share of compensation for insured losses under the Program shall be reduced by the amount of other compensation provided by other Federal programs to an insured or a third party to the extent such other compensation duplicates the insurance indemnification for those insured losses.

claims.quote: With respect to any underlying claim for insured losses, each insurer shall inquire of all involved policyholders, insureds, and claimants whether the person receiving insurance proceeds for an insured loss has received, expects to receive, or is entitled to receive compensation from another Federal program for the insured loss, and if so, the source and the amount of the compensation received or expected.
claims.summary: Each insurer shall inquire of all involved policyholders, insureds, and claimants whether the person receiving insurance proceeds for an insured loss has received, expects to receive, or is entitled to receive compensation from another Federal program for the insured loss, and if so, the source and the amount of the compensation received or expected.

claims.quote: Each insurer shall submit to Treasury a Notice on a form prescribed by Treasury whenever the insurer's aggregate insured losses (including reserves for “incurred but not reported” losses) within a calendar year exceed an amount equal to 50 percent of the insurer's deductible as specified in § 50.4(p).
claims.summary: Each insurer shall submit to Treasury a Notice on a form prescribed by Treasury whenever the insurer's aggregate insured losses (including reserves for “incurred but not reported” losses) within a calendar year exceed an amount equal to 50 percent of the insurer's deductible as specified in § 50.4(p).

claims.quote: The insurer shall file an Initial Certification of Loss, on a form prescribed by Treasury, and thereafter such Supplementary Certifications of Loss, on a form prescribed by Treasury, as may be necessary to receive payment for the Federal share of compensation for its insured losses.
claims.summary: The insurer must file an Initial Certification of Loss and any necessary Supplementary Certifications of Loss on forms prescribed by Treasury to receive payment for the Federal share of compensation for its insured losses.

claims.quote: An insurer shall use its best efforts to file with the Program the Initial Certification of Loss within 45 days following the last calendar day of the month when an insurer has paid aggregate insured losses that exceed its insurer deductible.
claims.summary: The insurer must use its best efforts to file the Initial Certification of Loss with the Program within 45 days following the last calendar day of the month when it has paid aggregate insured losses that exceed its insurer deductible.

claims.quote: The Initial Certification of Loss will include the following: (1) Basic information, on a form prescribed by Treasury, about each insured loss paid (or to be paid pursuant to § 50.73(b)(2)(i)) by the insurer. The form will include: (i) A listing of each insured loss paid (or to be paid pursuant to § 50,73(b)(2)(i)) by the insurer by catastrophe code and line of business; (ii) The total amount of reinsurance recovered from other sources; (iii) A calculation of the aggregate insured losses sustained by the insurer above its insurer deductible for the calendar year; and (iv) The amount the insurer claims as the Federal share of compensation for its aggregate insured losses.
claims.summary: The Initial Certification of Loss must include basic information about each insured loss paid or to be paid, including a listing by catastrophe code and line of business, the total amount of reinsurance recovered, a calculation of aggregate insured losses above the insurer deductible, and the amount claimed as the Federal share of compensation.

claims.quote: (2) A certification that the insurer is in compliance with the provisions of section 103(b) of the Act and this part, including certifications that: (i) The underlying insured losses reported pursuant to § 50.73(b)(1) either: Have been paid by the insurer; or will be paid by the insurer upon receipt of an advance payment of the Federal share of compensation as soon as possible, consistent with the insurer's normal business practices, but not longer than five business days after receipt of the Federal share of compensation; (ii) The underlying claims for insured losses were filed by persons who suffered an insured loss, or by persons acting on behalf of such persons; (iii) The underlying claims for insured losses were processed in accordance with appropriate business practices and the procedures specified in this subpart; (iv) The insurer has complied with the disclosure requirements of §§ 50.10 through 50.14, and the cap disclosure requirement of § 50.15, for each underlying insured loss that is included in the amount of the insurer's aggregate insured losses; and (v) The insurer has complied with the mandatory availability requirements of subpart C of this part.
claims.summary: The insurer must certify compliance with section 103(b) of the Act and this part, including that underlying insured losses are paid or will be paid within five business days of receiving the Federal share of compensation, claims were filed by persons who suffered an insured loss or their representatives, claims were processed in accordance with business practices and procedures, disclosure requirements of §§ 50.10 through 50.14 and the cap disclosure requirement of § 50.15 were met, and mandatory availability requirements of subpart C were met.

claims.quote: (3) A certification of the amount of the insurer's direct earned premium, together with the calculation of its insurer deductible (provided this certification was not submitted previously with the Notice of Deductible Erosion).
claims.summary: The insurer must certify the amount of its direct earned premium and the calculation of its insurer deductible, provided this certification was not submitted previously with the Notice of Deductible Erosion.

claims.quote: (4) A certification that the insurer will disburse payment of the Federal share of compensation in accordance with this Subpart.
claims.summary: The insurer must certify that it will disburse payment of the Federal share of compensation in accordance with this Subpart.

document_title: 31 CFR Part 50 (point-in-time 2026-07-01)

category: Title 31 — Code of Federal Regulations parts

claims.affected_party: every person engaging in any transaction subject to the provisions of this chapter
claims.quote: Except as otherwise provided, every person engaging in any transaction subject to the provisions of this chapter shall keep a full and accurate record of each such transaction engaged in, regardless of whether such transaction is effected pursuant to license or otherwise, and such record shall be available for examination for at least 10 years after the date of such transaction.
claims.summary: Every person engaging in a transaction subject to the provisions of this chapter must keep a full and accurate record of each such transaction, available for examination for at least 10 years after the transaction date.

claims.affected_party: every person holding property blocked pursuant to the provisions of this chapter or funds transfers retained pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter
claims.quote: Except as otherwise provided, every person holding property blocked pursuant to the provisions of this chapter or funds transfers retained pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter shall keep a full and accurate record of such property, and such record shall be available for examination for the period of time that such property is blocked and for at least 10 years after the date such property is unblocked.
claims.summary: Every person holding blocked property or funds transfers retained under § 596.504(b) must keep a full and accurate record of such property, available for examination during the blocking period and for at least 10 years after unblocking.

claims.quote: Every person is required to furnish under oath, in the form of reports or otherwise, from time to time and at any time as may be required by the Office of Foreign Assets Control, complete information relative to any act or transaction, regardless of whether such act or transaction is effected pursuant to license or otherwise, subject to the provisions of this chapter or relative to any property in which any foreign country or any national thereof has or had any interest of any nature whatsoever, direct or indirect.
claims.summary: Every person must furnish complete information under oath to OFAC regarding any act, transaction, or property subject to the provisions of this chapter.

claims.affected_party: Persons required to make such reports
claims.quote: The Office of Foreign Assets Control may require that such reports include the production of any books, contracts, letters, papers, or other hard copy or electronic documents relating to any such act, transaction, or property, in the custody or control of the persons required to make such reports.
claims.summary: OFAC may require the production of any books, contracts, letters, papers, or other hard copy or electronic documents relating to any such act, transaction, or property.

claims.quote: Persons providing documents to OFAC pursuant to this section must produce documents in a usable format agreed upon by OFAC.
claims.summary: Persons providing documents to OFAC must produce documents in a usable format agreed upon by OFAC.

claims.quote: If OFAC has reason to believe an account or transaction (or class of transactions) may involve the property or interests in property of a blocked person, OFAC may issue an instruction to one or more financial institutions that: (1) provides information or criteria to aid in the identification of blocked property; and (2) requires the financial institution to report transactions that meet the specified criteria and notify OFAC prior to processing such transactions.
claims.summary: OFAC may issue an instruction to financial institutions to report transactions that meet specified criteria and notify OFAC prior to processing such transactions.

claims.affected_party: U.S. person or person subject to U.S. jurisdiction
claims.quote: Any U.S. person (or person subject to U.S. jurisdiction in the case of part 515 of this chapter), including a financial institution, holding, unblocking, or transferring property blocked pursuant to this chapter shall submit the relevant reports described in this section to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
claims.summary: U.S. persons or those subject to U.S. jurisdiction must submit reports to OFAC when holding, unblocking, or transferring blocked property.

claims.affected_party: Persons holding, unblocking, or transferring blocked property
claims.quote: Reports shall be filed within 10 business days from the date that property becomes blocked.
claims.summary: Initial blocking reports must be filed within 10 business days from the date the property becomes blocked.

claims.quote: A report on all blocked property held as of June 30 of the current year shall be filed annually by September 30.
claims.summary: Annual reports on blocked property must be filed by September 30 of each year.

claims.affected_party: Persons unblocking or transferring blocked property
claims.quote: Reports shall be submitted to OFAC within 10 business days from the date blocked property is unblocked or transferred.
claims.summary: Reports on the release of property from blocked status must be submitted to OFAC within 10 business days from the date the property is unblocked or transferred.

claims.quote: The actual, or if unknown, estimated value of the property in U.S. Dollars. If the blocked property represents an outstanding loan, a credit card receivable, or other property with a negative balance, the amount blocked should be reported as $0.00 (zero) with the amount owed reflected in a narrative description.
claims.summary: The value of blocked property must be reported in U.S. Dollars, with specific instructions for negative balances.

claims.quote: The actual value of the property that was released from blocked status in U.S. Dollars. If the property represented an outstanding loan, a credit card receivable, or other property with a negative balance, the amount unblocked should be reported as $0.00 (zero) with the amount owed reflected in a narrative description.
claims.summary: The value of unblocked property must be reported in U.S. Dollars, with specific instructions for negative balances.

claims.quote: The legal authority or authorities under which the property is blocked. This may include a reference to the sanctions program (current programs are on OFAC's website: https://ofac.treasury.gov ), the applicable part of this chapter (e.g., 31 CFR part 515, 31 CFR part 544), an Executive order (E.O.) (e.g., E.O. 13224, E.O. 13599), or a statute (e.g., Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act).
claims.summary: The legal authority under which the property is blocked must be reported, including references to sanctions programs, parts of the chapter, Executive orders, or statutes.

claims.affected_party: Persons unblocking or transferring blocked property
claims.quote: The legal authority or authorities under which the property was unblocked or transferred. This may include, for example, reference to a specific or general license under an applicable part of this chapter or an E.O.
claims.summary: The legal authority under which the property was unblocked or transferred must be reported, including references to specific or general licenses or Executive orders.

claims.quote: A copy of any payment or transfer instructions, check, letter of credit, accompanying bill of lading, invoice, or any other relevant documentation received in connection with any related transaction.
claims.summary: A copy of any relevant documentation related to the transaction must be included in the report.

claims.affected_party: Persons unblocking or transferring blocked property
claims.quote: A copy of the original blocking report filed with OFAC pursuant to
claims.summary: A copy of the original blocking report filed with OFAC must be included in the report.

claims.quote: Except as otherwise provided, all initial reports of blocked property required under § 501.603(b)(1) and the Annual Reports of Blocked Property required under § 501.603(b)(2) must be filed electronically through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS), available on OFAC's website, https://ofac.treasury.gov/ofac-reporting-system.
claims.summary: Initial reports of blocked property and Annual Reports of Blocked Property must be filed electronically through the OFAC Reporting System.

claims.quote: A copy of reports submitted pursuant to this section shall be retained for the submitter's records.
claims.summary: A copy of reports submitted pursuant to this section must be retained for the submitter's records.

claims.quote: All reports of unblocked or transferred blocked property required pursuant to § 501.603(b)(3) must be submitted electronically to OFAC via email at OFACReport@treasury.gov, with the number of this section in the subject line, or through ORS, available on OFAC's website, https://ofac.treasury.gov/of,ofac-reporting-system.
claims.summary: All reports of unblocked or transferred blocked property required pursuant to § 501.603(b)(3) must be submitted electronically to OFAC via email or through ORS.

claims.quote: Information submitted to OFAC pursuant to this section will be protected from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552) and the provisions of 31 CFR part 1 if OFAC reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by a FOIA exemption or disclosure is prohibited by law.
claims.summary: Information submitted to OFAC pursuant to this section will be protected from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act if OFAC reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by a FOIA exemption or disclosure is prohibited by law.

claims.affected_party: U.S. person or person subject to U.S. jurisdiction
claims.quote: Any U.S. person (or person subject to U.S. jurisdiction in the case of part 515 of this chapter), including a financial institution, that rejects a transaction that is not blocked under the provisions of this chapter, but where processing or engaging in the transaction would nonetheless violate a provision contained in this chapter, shall submit a report to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
claims.summary: Persons rejecting transactions that are not blocked under the provisions of this chapter but would violate a provision contained in this chapter must submit a report to OFAC.

claims.quote: Reports of rejected transactions shall include the following information, to the extent the information is available to the person submitting the report at the time the transaction is rejected:
