claims.summary: Reports of rejected transactions must include specific information such as the name and address of the person rejecting the transaction, a description of the rejected transaction, associated sanctions targets, the date of rejection, the value of the property, legal authority, and related documentation.

claims.quote: Reports shall be filed within 10 business days of the rejected transaction prohibited by the provisions of this chapter.
claims.summary: Reports of rejected transactions must be filed within 10 business days of the transaction being prohibited by the provisions of this chapter.

claims.quote: Reports under this section shall be submitted to OFAC through the OFAC Reporting System, available on OFAC's website, https://ofac.treasury.gov/ofac-reporting-system.
claims.summary: Reports under this section must be submitted to OFAC through the OFAC Reporting System, available on OFAC's website.

claims.affected_party: U.S. persons or persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction
claims.quote: (a) U.S. persons (or persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction in the case of part 515 of this chapter) participating in litigation, arbitration, or other binding alternative dispute resolution proceedings in the United States on behalf of or against persons whose property or interests in property are blocked or whose funds have been retained pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter, or when the outcome of any proceeding may affect blocked property or retained funds, must: (1) Provide notice of such proceedings upon their commencement or upon submission or receipt of documents bringing the proceedings within the terms of the introductory text to this paragraph (a);
claims.summary: U.S. persons must provide notice of litigation, arbitration, or other binding alternative dispute resolution proceedings upon their commencement or upon submission or receipt of documents bringing the proceedings within the terms of the introductory text to this paragraph.

claims.affected_party: U.S. persons or persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction
claims.quote: (2) Submit copies of all pleadings, motions, memoranda, exhibits, stipulations, correspondence, and proposed orders or judgments (including any proposed final judgment or default judgment) submitted to the court or other adjudicatory body, and all orders, decisions, opinions, or memoranda issued by the court, to the Office of the Chief Counsel (Foreign Assets Control) at OFACReport@treasury.gov with the number of this section in the subject line, within 10 days of filing, submission, or issuance.
claims.summary: U.S. persons must submit copies of all pleadings, motions, memoranda, exhibits, stipulations, correspondence, and proposed orders or judgments submitted to the court or other adjud, and all orders, decisions, opinions, or memoranda issued by the court, to the Office of the Chief Counsel (Foreign Assets Control) within 10 days of filing, submission, or issuance.

claims.affected_party: U.S. persons or persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction
claims.quote: (3) Report by email to the Office of the Chief Counsel (Foreign Assets Control), at OFACReport@treasury.gov with the number of this section in the subject line, the scheduling of any hearing or status conference in the proceedings whenever it appears that the court or other adjudicatory body may issue an order or judgment in the proceedings (including a final judgment or default judgment) or is considering or may decide any pending request dispositive of the merits of the proceedings or of any claim raised in the proceedings.
claims.summary: U.S. persons must report by email to the Office of the Chief Counsel (Foreign Assets Control) the scheduling of any hearing or status conference in the proceedings whenever it appears that the court or other adjudicatory body may issue an order or judgment in the proceedings or is considering or may decide any pending request dispositive of the merits of the proceedings or of any claim raised in the proceedings.

claims.quote: (c) Persons initiating proceedings subject to the reporting requirements of this section must notify the court or other adjudicatory body of the restrictions set forth under the applicable part in this chapter governing the transfer of blocked property or funds retained pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter, including the prohibition on any unlicensed attachment, judgment, decree, lien, execution, garnishment or other judicial process with respect to any property in which, on or after the applicable effective date, there existed an interest of any person whose property and property interests were subject to blocking pursuant to this chapter or were subject to retention pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter.
claims.summary: Persons initiating proceedings must notify the court or other adjudicatory body of the restrictions set forth under the applicable part in this chapter governing the transfer of blocked property or funds retained pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter, including the prohibition on any unlicensed attachment, judgment, decree, lien, execution, garnishment or other judicial process with respect to any property in which, on or after the applicable effective date, there existed an interest of any person whose property and property interests were subject to blocking pursuant to this chapter or were subject to retention pursuant to § 596.504(b) of this chapter.

claims.quote: (1) Persons who willfully violate any provision of TWEA or any license, rule, or regulation issued thereunder, and persons who willfully violate, neglect, or refuse to comply with any order of the President issued in compliance with the provisions of TWEA shall, upon conviction, be fined not more than $1,000,000 or, if an individual, be imprisoned for not more than 20 years, or both.
claims.summary: Persons who willfully violate any provision of TWEA or any license, rule, or regulation issued thereunder, and persons who willfully violate, neglect, or refuse to comply with any order of the President issued in compliance with the provisions of TWEA shall be fined not more than $1,000,000 or, if an individual, be imprisoned for not more than 20 years, or both.

claims.quote: (2) Any property, funds, securities, papers, or other articles or documents, or any vessel, together with its tackle, apparel, furniture, and equipment, concerned in a violation of TWEA may upon conviction be forfeited to the United States Government.
claims.summary: Any property, funds, securities, papers, or other articles or documents, or any vessel, together with its tackle, apparel, furniture, and equipment, concerned in a violation of TWEA may be forfeited to the United States Government.

claims.quote: (3) The Secretary of the Treasury may impose a civil penalty of not more than $111,308 per violation on any person who violates any license, order, or regulation issued under TWEA.
claims.summary: The Secretary of the Treasury may impose a civil penalty of not more than $111,308 per violation on any person who violates any license, order, or regulation issued under TWEA.

claims.quote: (4) Any property, funds, securities, papers, or other articles or documents, or any vessel, together with its tackle, apparel, furniture, and equipment, that is the subject of a violation subject to a civil penalty issued pursuant to TWEA shall, at the discretion of the Secretary of the Treasury, be forfeited to the United States Government.
claims.summary: Any property, funds, securities, papers, or other articles or documents, or any vessel, together with its tackle, apparel, furniture, and equipment, that is the subject of a violation subject to a civil penalty issued pursuant to TWEA shall be forfeited to the United States Government.

claims.quote: (b) The criminal penalties provided in TWEA are subject to increase pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 3571 which, when read in conjunction with section 16 of TWEA, provides that persons convicted of violating TWEA may be fined up to the greater of either $250,000 for individuals and $1,000,000 for organizations or twice the pecuniary gain or loss from the violation.
claims.summary: The criminal penalties provided in TWEA are subject to increase pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 3571 which, when read in conjunction with section 16 of TWEA, provides that persons convicted of violating TWEA may be fined up to the greater of either $250,000 for individuals and $1,000,000 for organizations or twice the pecuniary gain or loss from the violation.

claims.quote: (c) Attention is directed to 18 U.S.C. 1001, which provides that whoever, in any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States, knowingly and willfully falsifies, conceals or covers up by any trick, scheme, or device a material fact, or makes any false, fictitious or fraudulent statements or representations, or makes or uses any false writing or document knowing the same to contain any false, fictitious or fraudulent statement or entry, shall be fined under title 18, United States Code, or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.
claims.summary: Whoever, in any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States, knowingly and willfully falsifies, conceals or covers up by any trick, scheme, or device a material fact, or makes any false, fictitious or fraudulent statements or representations, or makes or uses any false writing or document knowing the same to contain any false, fictitious or fraudulent statement or entry, shall be fined under title 18, United States Code, or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.

claims.quote: The Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control will notify a suspected violator (hereinafter “respondent”) of an alleged violation by issuing a “Prepenalty Notice.” The Prepenalty Notice shall describe the alleged violation(s) and include a proposed civil penalty amount.
claims.summary: The Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control must notify a suspected violator of an alleged violation by issuing a Prepenalty Notice, which must describe the alleged violation(s) and include a proposed civil penalty amount.

claims.quote: The respondent will have 60 days from the date the Prepenalty Notice is served to make a written presentation either defending against the alleged violation or admitting the violation.
claims.summary: The respondent must make a written presentation within 60 days from the date the Prepenalty Notice is served, either defending against the alleged violation or admitting the violation.

claims.quote: A respondent who admits a violation may offer information as to why a monetary penalty should not be imposed or why, if imposed, the monetary penalty should be in a lesser amount than proposed.
claims.summary: A respondent who admits a violation may offer information as to why a monetary penalty should not be imposed or why, if imposed, the monetary penalty should be in a lesser amount than proposed.

claims.quote: The Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control will issue a “Penalty Notice.” The respondent will have 30 days from the date of service to either pay the penalty or request a hearing.
claims.summary: The respondent must either pay the penalty or request a hearing within 30 days from the date of service of the Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: If the respondent requests a hearing, the Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control will have two options: (i) The Director may issue an “Order Instituting Proceedings” and refer the matter to an Administrative Law Judge for a hearing and decision; or (ii) The Director may determine to discontinue the penalty action based on information presented by the respondent.
claims.summary: If the respondent requests a hearing, the Director of the Office of Foreign Assets Control may issue an Order Instituting Proceedings and refer the matter to an Administrative Law Judge for a hearing and decision, or may determine to discontinue the penalty action based on information presented by the respondent.

claims.quote: The respondent may seek judicial review of the final decision of the Department.
claims.summary: The respondent may seek judicial review of the final decision of the Department.

claims.quote: No person shall be represented before the Director in any civil penalty matter, or an Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee in a civil penalty hearing, under this subpart except as provided in this section.
claims.summary: A person cannot be represented before the Director in a civil penalty matter or hearing unless it is provided for in this section.

claims.quote: A respondent may be represented by a personal representative. If a respondent wishes to be represented by counsel, such counsel must be an attorney at law admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of the United States, the highest court of any State, commonwealth, possession, or territory of the United States, or the District of Columbia;
claims.summary: A respondent may be represented by a personal representative or counsel, who must be an attorney admitted to practice before specific courts.

claims.quote: The Director shall be represented by members of the Office of Chief Counsel or any other counsel specifically assigned by the General Counsel.
claims.summary: The Director must be represented by members of the Office of Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel.

claims.quote: No individual shall appear as representative for a respondent in a proceeding conducted pursuant to this subpart if it reasonably appears that such representation may be materially limited by that representative's responsibilities to a third person, or by that representative's own interests.
claims.summary: An individual cannot appear as a representative for a respondent if their representation is materially limited by their responsibilities to a third person or their own interests.

claims.quote: The Director shall cause any Prepenalty Notice, Penalty Notice, Acknowledgment of Hearing Request, Order Instituting Proceedings, and other related orders and decisions, or any amendments or supplements thereto, to be served upon the respondent.
claims.summary: The Director must serve the Prepenalty Notice, Penalty Notice, Acknowledgment of Hearing Request, Order Instituting Proceedings, and other related orders and decisions on the respondent.

claims.quote: Service shall be complete: (i) Upon the date of mailing by first class (regular) mail to the respondent at the respondent's last known address, or to a representative authorized to receive service, including qualified representatives noticed to the Director pursuant to § 501.704. Absent satisfactory evidence in the administrative record to the contrary, the Director may presume that the date of mailing is the date stamped on the first page of the notice or order. The respondent may rebut the presumption that a notice or order was mailed on the stamped mailing date only by presenting evidence of the postmark date on the envelope in which the notice or order was mailed;
claims.summary: The Director must serve the notice or order by first class mail to the respondent's last known address or a representative, and the date of mailing is presumed to be the date stamped on the notice or order unless rebutted by evidence of the postmark date.

claims.quote: If the Director has reason to believe there has occurred a violation of any provision of parts 500 or 515 of this chapter or a violation of the provisions of any license, ruling, regulation, order, direction or instruction issued by or pursuant to the direction or authorization of the Secretary pursuant to parts 500 or 515 of this chapter or otherwise under the Trading With the Enemy Act, and the Director determines that further civil proceedings are warranted, the Director shall issue a Prepenalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Director must issue a Prepenalty Notice if there is a violation of certain provisions and further civil proceedings are warranted.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall describe the alleged violation, specify the laws and regulations allegedly violated, and state the amount of the proposed monetary penalty.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must describe the alleged violation, specify the laws and regulations allegedly violated, and state the amount of the proposed monetary penalty.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall inform the respondent of respondent's right to make a written presentation within the time prescribed in § 501.707 as to why the respondent believes there should be no finding of a violation or why, if the respondent admits the violation, a monetary penalty should not be imposed or why, if imposed, the monetary penalty should be in a lesser amount than proposed.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must inform the respondent of their right to make a written presentation within the time prescribed in § 501.707.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall also inform the respondent that: (i) The act of submitting a written response by the respondent is a factor that may result in a lower penalty absent any aggravating factors; and (ii) If the respondent fails to respond to the Prepenalty Notice within the applicable 60-day period set forth in § 501.707, the Director may proceed with the issuance of a Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must inform the respondent that submitting a written response may result in a lower penalty and that failure to respond within 60 days may lead to the issuance of a Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall inform the respondent of respondent's right, if a subsequent Penalty Notice is issued, to request an administrative hearing. The Director will not consider any request for an administrative hearing until a Penalty Notice has been issued.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must inform the respondent of their right to request an administrative hearing if a subsequent Penalty Notice is issued, and the Director will not consider such a request until a Penalty Notice has been issued.

claims.quote: The respondent shall have 60 days after the date of service of the Prepenalty Notice pursuant to § 501.705(a) to respond thereto.
claims.summary: The respondent must respond to the Prepenalty Notice within 60 days after the date of service.

claims.quote: The response, signed and dated, shall be served as provided in
claims.summary: The response must be signed and dated and served as provided in the relevant section.

claims.quote: (2) The failure to submit a response within the time period set forth in this paragraph (a), including any additional time granted by the Director, shall be deemed to be a waiver of the right to respond to the Prepenalty Notice.
claims.summary: Failure to submit a response within the time period set forth in this paragraph (a), including any additional time granted by the Director, shall be deemed to be a waiver of the right to respond to the Prepenalty Notice.

claims.quote: (i) The response must admit or deny specifically each separate allegation of violation made in the Prepenalty Notice. If the respondent is without knowledge as to an allegation, the response shall so state, and such statement shall constitute a denial. Any allegation not specifically addressed in the response shall be deemed admitted.
claims.summary: The response must admit or deny specifically each separate allegation of violation made in the Prepenalty Notice. If the respondent is without knowledge as to an allegation, the response shall so state, and such statement shall constitute a denial. Any allegation not specifically addressed in the response shall be deemed admitted.

claims.quote: (ii) The response must set forth any additional or new matter or arguments the respondent seeks, or shall seek, to use in support of all defenses or claims for mitigation. Any defense the respondent wishes to assert must be included in the response.
claims.summary: The response must set forth any additional or new matter or arguments the respondent seeks, or shall seek, to use in support of all defenses or claims for mitigation. Any defense the respondent wishes to assert must be included in the response.

claims.quote: (iii) The response must accurately state (for each respondent, if applicable) the respondent's full name and address for future service, together with a current telephone and, if applicable, facsimile machine number. If respondent is represented, the representative's full name and address, together with telephone and facsimile numbers, may be provided instead of service information for the respondent. The respondent or respondent's representative of record is responsible for providing timely written notice to the Director of any subsequent changes in the information provided.
claims.summary: The response must accurately state (for each respondent, if applicable) the respondent's full name and address for future service, together with a current telephone and, if applicable, facsimile machine number. If respondent is represented, the representative's full name and address, together with telephone and facsimile numbers, may be provided instead of service information for the respondent. The respondent or respondent's representative of record is responsible for providing timely written notice to the Director of any subsequent changes in the information provided.

claims.quote: (iv) Financial disclosure statement requirement. Any respondent who asserts financial hardship or an inability to pay a penalty shall include with the response a financial disclosure statement setting forth in detail the basis for asserting the financial hardship or inability to pay a penalty, subject to 18 U.S.C. 1001.
claims.summary: Any respondent who asserts financial hardship or an inability to pay a penalty shall include with the response a financial disclosure statement setting forth in detail the basis for asserting the financial hardship or inability to pay a penalty, subject to 18 U.S.C. 1001.

claims.quote: In the event of settlement prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice, the claim proposed in the Prepenalty Notice will be withdrawn and the respondent will not be required to make a written response to the Prepenalty Notice. In the event no settlement is reached, a written response to the Prepenalty Notice is required pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.
claims.summary: In the event of settlement prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice, the claim proposed in the Prepenalty Notice will be withdrawn and the respondent will not be required to make a written response to the Prepenalty Notice. In the event no settlement is reached, a written response to the Prepenalty Notice is required pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.

claims.quote: If after considering any written response to the Prepenalty Notice submitted pursuant to § 501.707 and any other relevant facts, the Director determines that there was no violation or that the violation does not warrant the imposition of a civil monetary penalty, the Director promptly shall notify the respondent in writing of that determination and that no civil monetary penalty pursuant to this subpart will be imposed.
claims.summary: If after considering any written response to the Prepenalty Notice submitted pursuant to § 501.707 and any other relevant facts, the Director determines that there was no violation or that the violation does not warrant the imposition of a civil monetary penalty, the Director promptly shall notify the respondent in writing of that determination and that no civil monetary penalty pursuant to this subpart will be imposed.

claims.quote: The Director promptly shall issue a Penalty Notice informing the respondent that, absent a timely request for an administrative hearing, the Director will impose the civil monetary penalty described in the Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Director must issue a Penalty Notice if a violation is determined and a monetary penalty is warranted.

claims.quote: The Penalty Notice shall inform the respondent: (1) Of the respondent's right to submit a written request for an administrative hearing not later than 3,0 days after the date of service of the Penalty Notice;
claims.summary: The Penalty Notice must inform the respondent of their right to submit a written request for an administrative hearing within 30 days.

claims.quote: (2) That in the absence of a timely request for a hearing, the issuance of the Penalty Notice constitutes final agency action;
claims.summary: The issuance of the Penalty Notice constitutes final agency action if no timely request for a hearing is made.

claims.quote: (3) That, absent a timely request for a hearing, payment (or arrangement with the Financial Management Service of the Department for installment payment) of the assessed penalty must be made not later than 30 days after the date of service of the Penalty Notice;
claims.summary: Payment of the assessed penalty or an arrangement for installment payment must be made within 30 days if no timely request for a hearing is made.

claims.quote: (4) That absent a timely request for a hearing, the respondent must furnish respondent's taxpayer identification number pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 7701 and that the Director intends to use such information for the purposes of collecting and reporting on any delinquent penalty amount in the event of a failure to pay the penalty imposed.
claims.summary: The respondent must furnish their taxpayer identification number if no timely request for a hearing is made, and the Director intends to use this information for collecting and reporting delinquent penalties.

claims.quote: Either the Director or any respondent may, at any time during the administrative civil penalty process described in this subpart, propose an offer of settlement.
claims.summary: Either the Director or any respondent may propose an offer of settlement at any time during the administrative civil penalty process.

claims.quote: The amount accepted in settlement may be less than the civil penalty that might be imposed in the event of a formal determination of violation.
claims.summary: The amount accepted in settlement may be less than the civil penalty that might be imposed in the event of a formal determination of violation.

claims.quote: Upon mutual agreement by the Director and a respondent on the terms of a settlement, the Director shall issue an Order of Settlement.
claims.summary: Upon mutual agreement by the Director and a respondent on the terms of a settlement, the Director shall issue an Order of Settlement.

claims.quote: Any offer of settlement made by a respondent prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice shall be submitted, in writing, to the Chief of Civil Penalties, Office of Foreign Assets Control, U.S. Department of the Treasury, 1500 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW., Washington, DC 20220.
claims.summary: Any offer of settlement made by a respondent prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice shall be submitted, in writing, to the Chief of Civil Penalties, Office of Foreign Assets Control, U.S. Department of the Treasury, 1500 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW., Washington, DC 20220.

claims.quote: Any offer of settlement made by a respondent after issuance of a Penalty Notice shall state that it is made pursuant to this section; shall recite or incorporate as a part of the offer the provisions of paragraphs (b)(5)(ii) and (b)(6) of this section; shall be signed by the respondent making the offer, and not only by his or her representative; and shall be submitted to the Chief Counsel.
claims.summary: Any offer of settlement made by a respondent after issuance of a Penalty Notice shall state that it is made pursuant to this section; shall recite or incorporate as a part of the offer the provisions of paragraphs (b)(5)(ii) and (b)(6) of this section; shall be signed by the respondent making the offer, and not only by his or her representative; and shall be submitted to the Chief Counsel.

claims.quote: The submission of any settlement offer does not provide a basis for adjourning or otherwise delaying all or any portion of the administrative civil penalty process.
claims.summary: The submission of any settlement offer does not provide a basis for adjourning or otherwise delaying all or any portion of the administrative civil penalty process.

claims.quote: Any respondent (or potential respondent in the case of a pending Prepenalty Notice) may request, in writing, that the Director withhold issuance of any such notice, or grant an extension of time to respond to any such Notice, for a period not to exceed 60 days for the exclusive purpose of effecting settlement.
claims.summary: Any respondent (or potential respondent in the case of a pending Prepenalty Notice) may request, in writing, that the Director withhold issuance of any such notice, or grant an extension of time to respond to any such Notice, for a period not to exceed 60 days for the exclusive purpose of effecting settlement.

claims.quote: The Director may grant any such request, in writing, under terms and conditions within his or her discretion.
claims.summary: The Director may grant any such request, in writing, under terms and conditions within his or her discretion.

claims.quote: Upon mutual agreement of the Director and a respondent, the Administrative Law Judge may grant an extension of time, for a period not to exceed 60 days, for the exclusive purpose of effecting settlement.
claims.summary: Upon mutual agreement of the Director and a respondent, the Administrative Law Judge may grant an extension of time, for a period not to exceed 60 days, for the exclusive purpose of effecting settlement.

claims.quote: Where an Administrative Law Judge is assigned to a proceeding, the Director or the respondent may request that the Administrative Law Judge express his or her views regarding the appropriateness of the offer of settlement.
claims.summary: Where an Administrative Law Judge is assigned to a proceeding, the Director or the respondent may request that the Administrative Law Judge express his or her views regarding the appropriateness of the offer of settlement.

claims.quote: A request for the Administrative Law Judge to express his or her views on an offer of settlement or otherwise to participate in a settlement conference constitutes a waiver by the party making the request of any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Administrative Law Judge based on the views expressed.
claims.summary: A request for the Administrative Law Judge to express his or her views on an offer of settlement or otherwise to participate in a settlement conference constitutes a waiver by the party making the request of any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Administrative Law Judge based on the views expressed.

claims.quote: By submitting an offer of settlement, a respondent making the offer waives, subject to acceptance of the offer: (A) All hearings pursuant to section 16 of the Trading with the Enemy Act (50 U.S.C. App. 16); (B) The filing of proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law; (C) Proceedings before, and a decision by, an Administrative Law Judge; (D) All post-hearing procedures; and (E) Judicial review by any court.
claims.summary: By submitting an offer of settlement, a respondent making the offer waives, subject to acceptance of the offer: (A) All hearings pursuant to section 16 of the Trading with the Enemy Act (50 U.S.C. App. 16); (B) The filing of proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law; (C) Proceedings before, and a decision by, an Administrative Law Judge; (D) All post-hearing procedures; and (E) Judicial review by any court.

claims.quote: By submitting an offer of settlement the respondent further waives: (A) Such provisions of this subpart or other requirements of law as may be construed to prevent any member of the Director's staff, or members of the Office of Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel, from participating in or advising the Director as to any order, opinion, finding of fact, or conclusion of law to be entered pursuant to the offer; and (B) Any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Director based on the consideration of or discussions concerning settlement of all or any part of the proceeding.
claims.summary: By submitting an offer of settlement the respondent further waives: (A) Such provisions of this subpart or other requirements of law as may be construed to prevent any member of the Director's staff, or members of the Office of Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel, from participating in or advising the Director as to any order, opinion, finding of fact, or conclusion of law to be entered pursuant to the offer; and (B) Any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Director based on the consideration of or discussions concerning settlement of all or any part of the proceeding.

claims.quote: If the Director rejects the offer of settlement, the respondent shall be so notified in writing and the offer of settlement shall be deemed withdrawn.
claims.summary: If the Director rejects the offer of settlement, the respondent shall be so notified in writing and the offer of settlement shall be deemed withdrawn.

claims.quote: The rejected offer shall not constitute a part of the record in any proceeding against the respondent making the offer, provided, however, that rejection of an offer of settlement does not affect the continued validity of waivers pursuant to paragraph (b)(5) of this section with respect to any discussions concerning the rejected offer of settlement.
claims.summary: The rejected offer shall not constitute a part of the record in any proceeding against the respondent making the offer, provided, however, that rejection of an offer of settlement does not affect the continued validity of waivers pursuant to paragraph (b)(5) of this section with respect to any discussions concerning the rejected offer of settlement.

claims.quote: No settlement offer or proposal, or any subsequent negotiation or resolution, is admissible as evidence in any administrative proceeding initiated by the Director.
claims.summary: No settlement offer or proposal, or any subsequent negotiation or resolution, is admissible as evidence in any administrative proceeding initiated by the Director.

claims.quote: A request for an agency hearing shall be served on the Director not later than 30 days after the date of service of the Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: A respondent must request an agency hearing within 30 days of the Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: A respondent may not reserve the right to request a hearing after expiration of the 30 calendar day period.
claims.summary: A respondent cannot reserve the right to request a hearing after the 30-day period.

claims.quote: A request for a hearing that is not made as required by this paragraph shall constitute a waiver of the respondent's right to a hearing.
claims.summary: Failure to make a hearing request as required constitutes a waiver of the right to a hearing.

claims.quote: The request need not be in any particular form, but must be typewritten and contain the heading “Request for Agency Hearing”.
claims.summary: The hearing request must be typewritten and include the heading 'Request for Agency Hearing'.

claims.quote: The request must include the Office of Foreign Assets Control identification number shown near the top of the Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The hearing request must include the OFAC identification number from the Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: The request must accurately state, for each respondent (if applicable), the respondent's full name and address for future service, together with current telephone and, if applicable, a facsimile machine number.
claims.summary: The hearing request must include the respondent's full name, address, telephone number, and facsimile number.

claims.quote: The respondent or respondent's representative is responsible for providing timely written notice to the Director of any subsequent changes in the information provided.
claims.summary: The respondent or representative must provide timely written notice of any changes to the information provided.

claims.quote: The respondent or, if represented, the respondent's representative, must sign the hearing request.
claims.summary: The respondent or their representative must sign the hearing request.

claims.quote: No later than 60 days after service of any hearing request, the Director shall acknowledge receipt and inform a respondent, in writing, whether an Order Instituting Proceedings shall be issued.
claims.summary: The Director must acknowledge receipt of a hearing request and inform the respondent in writing within 60 days.

claims.quote: If a respondent makes a timely request for a hearing, the Director shall determine, at his or her option, whether to dismiss the violation(s) set forth in the Penalty Notice or to issue an Order Instituting Proceedings to initiate the hearing process.
claims.summary: The Director must determine whether to dismiss the violation or issue an Order Instituting Proceedings if a timely hearing request is made.

claims.quote: The respondent shall file, with the Administrative Law Judge and the Office of Chief Counsel, an answer to each of the allegations contained therein.
claims.summary: The respondent must file an answer to each allegation in the Order Instituting Proceedings.

claims.quote: A respondent may file with an answer a motion for a more definite statement of specified matters of fact or law to be considered or determined.
claims.summary: A respondent may file a motion for a more definite statement of specified matters of fact or law.

claims.quote: A respondent may amend its answer at any time by written consent of the Director or with permission of the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: A respondent may amend its answer with written consent of the Director or permission of the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: The Director may, in his or her discretion, withdraw an Order Instituting Proceedings at any time prior to the issuance of a decision by the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: The Director may withdraw an Order Instituting Proceedings at any time prior to the issuance of a decision by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: The Director may combine claims contained in two or more Penalty Notices involving the same respondent, and for which hearings have been requested, into a single Order Instituting Proceedings.
claims.summary: The Director may combine claims from two or more Penalty Notices involving the same respondent into a single Order Instituting Proceedings.

claims.quote: Upon motion by the Director, the Administrative Law Judge may, at any time prior to issuance of a decision, permit the Director to amend an Order Instituting Proceedings to include new matters of fact or law that are within the scope of the original Order Instituting Proceedings.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge may permit the Director to amend an Order Instituting Proceedings to include new matters of fact or law within the original scope.

claims.quote: The Order Instituting Proceedings shall: (1) Be prepared by the Office of the Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel and based on information provided by the Director;
claims.summary: The Order Instituting Proceedings must be prepared by the Office of the Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel and based on information provided by the Director.

claims.quote: The Order Instituting Proceedings shall: (2) State the legal authority under which the hearing is to be held;
claims.summary: The Order Instituting Proceedings must state the legal authority under which the hearing is to be held.

claims.quote: The Order Instituting Proceedings shall: (3) Contain a short and plain statement of the alleged violation(s) to be considered and determined (including the matters of fact and law asserted) in such detail as will permit a specific response thereto;
claims.summary: The Order Instituting Proceedings must contain a short and plain statement of the alleged violation(s) to be considered and determined in such detail as will permit a specific response thereto.

claims.quote: The Order Instituting Proceedings shall: (4) State the amount of the penalty sought in the proceeding;
claims.summary: The Order Instituting Proceedings must state the amount of the penalty sought in the proceeding.

claims.quote: The Order Instituting Proceedings shall: (5) Be signed by the Director.
claims.summary: The Order Instituting Proceedings must be signed by the Director.

claims.quote: If the Director issues an Order Instituting Proceedings, the respondent shall receive not less than 45 days notice of the time and place of the hearing.
claims.summary: The respondent must receive at least 45 days notice of the time and place of the hearing.

claims.quote: All hearings shall be held in the Washington, DC metropolitan area unless, based on extraordinary reasons, otherwise mutually agreed by the respondent and the Director.
claims.summary: Hearings must be held in the Washington, DC metropolitan area unless otherwise agreed upon by the respondent and the Director.

claims.quote: The time for any hearing shall be fixed with due regard for the public interest and the convenience and necessity of the parties or their representatives.
claims.summary: The time for any hearing must be fixed with due regard for the public interest and the convenience and necessity of the parties or their representatives.

claims.quote: Requests to change the time of a hearing may be submitted to the Administrative Law Judge, who may modify the hearing date(s) and/or time(s) and place.
claims.summary: Requests to change the time of a hearing may be submitted to the Administrative Law Judge, who may modify the hearing date(s) and/or time(s) and place.

claims.quote: All requests for a change in the date and time and/or place of a hearing must be received by the Administrative Law Judge and served upon the parties no later than 15 days before the scheduled hearing date.
claims.summary: All requests for a change in the date and time and/or place of a hearing must be received by the Administrative Law Judge and served upon the parties no later than 15 days before the scheduled hearing date.

claims.quote: Any respondent named in an order instituting proceedings as a person against whom findings may be made or penalties imposed who fails to appear (in person or through a representative) at a hearing of which he or she has been duly notified may be deemed to be in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).
claims.summary: Any respondent who fails to appear at a hearing of which they have been duly notified may be deemed to be in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).

claims.quote: A respondent may make a motion to set aside a default pursuant to § 501.726(e).
claims.summary: A respondent may make a motion to set aside a default pursuant to § 501.726(e).

claims.quote: A party to a proceeding may be deemed to be in default and the Administrative Law Judge (or the Secretary's designee during review proceedings) may determine the proceeding against that party upon consideration of the record if that party fails: (1) To appear, in person or through a representative, at any hearing or conference of which the party has been notified; (2) To answer, to respond to a dispositive motion within the time provided, or otherwise to prosecute or defend the proceeding; or (3) To cure a deficient filing within the time specified by the Administrative Law Judge (or the Secretary's designee) pursuant to § 501.729(b).
claims.summary: A party may be deemed to be in default if they fail to appear at a hearing or conference, answer or respond to a dispositive motion, or cure a deficient filing within the specified time.

claims.quote: In deciding whether to determine the proceedings against a party deemed to be in default, the Administrative Law Judge shall consider the record of the proceedings (including the Order Instituting Proceedings) and shall construe contested matters of fact and law against the party deemed to be in default.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge shall consider the record of the proceedings and construe contested matters of fact and law against the party deemed to be in default.

claims.quote: For information and procedures pertaining to a motion to set aside a default, see § 501.726(e).
claims.summary: For information and procedures pertaining to a motion to set aside a default, see § 501.726(e).

claims.quote: By order of the Administrative Law Judge, proceedings involving common questions of law and fact may be consolidated for hearing of any or all the matters at issue in such proceedings.
claims.summary: Proceedings involving common questions of law and fact may be consolidated for hearing of any or all the matters at issue in such proceedings.

claims.quote: The Administrative Law Judge may make such orders concerning the conduct of such proceedings as he or she deems appropriate to avoid unnecessary cost or delay.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge may make such orders concerning the conduct of such proceedings as he or she deems appropriate to avoid unnecessary cost or delay.

claims.quote: All hearings shall be conducted in a fair, impartial, expeditious and orderly manner.
claims.summary: All hearings shall be conducted in a fair, impartial, expeditious and orderly manner.

claims.quote: Each party has the right to present its case or defense by oral and documentary evidence and to conduct such cross examination as may be required for full disclosure of the relevant facts.
claims.summary: Each party has the right to present its case or defense by oral and documentary evidence and to conduct such cross examination as may be required for full disclosure of the relevant facts.

claims.quote: The Director shall present his or her case-in-chief first.
claims.summary: The Director shall present his or her case-in-chief first.

claims.quote: The Director shall be the first party to present an opening statement and a closing statement and may make a rebuttal statement after the respondent's closing statement.
claims.summary: The Director shall be the first party to present an opening statement and a closing statement and may make a rebuttal statement after the respondent's closing statement.

claims.affected_party: party, interested person, or representative thereof
claims.quote: From the time the Director issues an Order Instituting Proceedings until the date of final decision, no party, interested person, or representative thereof shall knowingly make or cause to be made an ex parte communication.
claims.summary: Prohibition on ex parte communications during proceedings.

claims.affected_party: Secretary's designee and the Administrative Law Judge presiding over any proceeding
claims.quote: Except to the extent required for the disposition of ex parte communication matters as authorized by law, the Secretary's designee and the Administrative Law Judge presiding over any proceeding may not: (i) Consult a person or party on an issue, unless on notice and opportunity for all parties to participate; or (ii) Be responsible to or subject to the supervision, direction of, or evaluation by, an employee engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecutorial functions for the Department.
claims.summary: Prohibition on consultation or supervision by certain officials regarding investigative or prosecutorial functions.

claims.affected_party: Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee
claims.quote: If an ex parte communication is received by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, the Administrative Law, Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate, shall cause all of such written communication (or, if the communication is oral, a memorandum stating the substance of the communication) to be placed on the record of the proceeding and served on all parties.
claims.summary: Requirement to place ex parte communication on the record and serve it on all parties.

claims.quote: A party may, not later than 10 days after the date of service, file a response thereto and may recommend that the person making the prohibited communication be sanctioned pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.
claims.summary: Requirement to file a response within 10 days and recommend sanctions for prohibited communication.

claims.affected_party: party to the proceeding, a party's representative, or any other interested individual
claims.quote: Any party to the proceeding, a party's representative, or any other interested individual, who makes a prohibited ex parte communication, or who encourages or solicits another to make any such communication, may be subject to any appropriate sanction or sanctions imposed by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate, for good cause shown, including, but not limited to, exclusion from the hearing and an adverse ruling on the issue that is the subject of the prohibited communication.
claims.summary: Prohibition on making or encouraging prohibited ex parte communications, with potential sanctions.

claims.affected_party: officer or employee engaged in investigative or prosecutorial functions
claims.quote: Any officer or employee engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecutorial functions for the Department in a proceeding as defined in § 501.702 may not, in that proceeding or one that is factually related, participate or advise in the decision pursuant to Section 557 of the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. 557, except as a witness or counsel in the proceeding.
claims.summary: Prohibition on participation or advising in decisions by officers or employees engaged in investigative or prosecutorial functions.

claims.affected_party: Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee
claims.quote: All hearings, except hearings on applications for confidential treatment filed pursuant to § 501.725(b), shall be public unless otherwise ordered by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate, on his or her own motion or the motion of a party.
claims.summary: Requirement to make hearings public unless otherwise ordered.

claims.quote: The Administrative Law Judge may direct a representative or any party to attend one or more prehearing conferences.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge may direct a representative or any party to attend one or more prehearing conferences.

claims.quote: Such conferences may be held with or without the Administrative Law Judge present as the Administrative Law Judge deems appropriate.
claims.summary: Such conferences may be held with or without the Administrative Law Judge present as the Administrative Law Judge deems appropriate.

claims.quote: Where such a conference is held outside the presence of the Administrative Law Judge, the Administrative Law Judge shall be advised promptly by the parties of any agreements reached.
claims.summary: Where such a conference is held outside the presence of the Administrative Law Judge, the Administrative Law Judge shall be advised promptly by the parties of any agreements reached.

claims.quote: Such conferences also may be held with one or more persons participating by telephone or other remote means.
claims.summary: Such conferences also may be held with one or more persons participating by telephone or other remote means.

claims.quote: At a prehearing conference consideration may be given and action taken with respect to the following: (1) Simplification and clarification of the issues; (2) Exchange of witness and exhibit lists and copies of exhibits; (3) Admissions of fact and stipulations concerning the contents, authenticity, or admissibility into evidence of documents; (4) Matters of which official notice may be taken; (5) The schedule for exchanging prehearing motions or briefs, if any; (6) The method of service for papers; (7) Summary disposition of any or all issues; (8) Settlement of any or all issues; (9) Determination of hearing dates (when the Administrative Law Judge is present); (10) Amendments to the Order Instituting Proceedings or answers thereto; (11) Production of documents as set forth in § 501.723, and prehearing production of documents in response to subpoenas duces tecum as set forth in § 501.728; and (12) Such other matters as may aid in the orderly and expeditious disposition of the proceeding.
claims.summary: At a prehearing conference consideration may be given and action taken with respect to the following: (1) Simplification and clarification of the issues; (2) Exchange of witness and exhibit lists and copies of exhibits; (3) Admissions of fact and stipulations concerning the contents, authenticity, or admissibility into evidence of documents; (4) Matters of which official notice may be taken; (5) The schedule for exchanging prehearing motions or briefs, if any; (6) The method of service for papers; (7) Summary disposition of any or all issues; (8) Settlement of any or all issues; (9) Determination of hearing dates (when the Administrative Law Judge is present); (10) Amendments to the Order Instituting Proceedings or answers thereto; (11) Production of documents as set forth in § 501.723, and prehearing production of documents in response to subpoenas duces tecum as set forth in § 501.728; and (12) Such other matters as may aid in the orderly and expeditious disposition of the proceeding.

claims.quote: Unless the Administrative Law Judge orders otherwise, an initial prehearing conference shall be held not later than 14 days after service of an answer.
claims.summary: Unless the Administrative Law Judge orders otherwise, an initial prehearing conference shall be held not later than 14 days after service of an answer.

claims.quote: A final conference, if any, should be held as close to the start of the hearing as reasonable under the circumstances.
claims.summary: A final conference, if any, should be held as close to the start of the hearing as reasonable under the circumstances.

claims.quote: At or following the conclusion of any conference held pursuant to this rule, the Administrative Law Judge shall enter written rulings or orders that recite the agreement(s) reached and any procedural determinations made by the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: At or following the conclusion of any conference held pursuant to this rule, the Administrative Law Judge shall enter written rulings or orders that recite the agreement(s) reached and any procedural determinations made by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: A respondent who fails to appear, in person or through a representative, at a prehearing conference of which he or she has been duly notified may be deemed in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).
claims.summary: A respondent who fails to appear, in person or through a representative, at a prehearing conference of which he or she has been duly notified may be deemed in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).

claims.quote: A respondent may make a motion to set aside a default pursuant to § 501.726(e).
claims.summary: A respondent may make a motion to set aside a default pursuant to § 501.726(e).

claims.quote: a party shall, without awaiting a discovery request, provide to the opposing party: (i) The name and, if known, the address and telephone number of each individual likely to have discoverable information that the disclosing party may use to support its claims or defenses, unless solely for impeachment of a witness appearing in person or by deposition, identifying the subjects of the information; and (ii) A copy, or a description by category and location, of all documents, data compilations, and tangible things that are in the possession, custody, or control of the party and that the disclosing party may use to support its claims or defenses, unless solely for impeachment of a witness appearing in person or by deposition;
claims.summary: A party must provide the opposing party with information about individuals likely to have discoverable information and a description of all documents, data compilations, and tangible things that the party may use to support its claims or defenses.

claims.quote: The disclosures described in paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section shall be made not later than 30 days after the issuance of an Order Instituting Proceedings, unless a different time is set by stipulation or by order of the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: The disclosures described in paragraph (a)(1)(i) must be made not later than 30 days after the issuance of an Order Instituting Proceedings, unless a different time is set by stipulation or by order of the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: In addition to the disclosures required by paragraph (a) of this section, a party must provide to the opposing party, and promptly file with the Administrative Law Judge, the following information regarding the evidence that it may present at hearing for any purpose other than solely for impeachment of a witness appearing in person or by deposition: (i) An outline or narrative summary of its case or defense (the Order Instituting Proceedings will usually satisfy this requirement for the Director and the answer thereto will usually satisfy this requirement for the respondent); (ii) The legal theories upon which it will rely; (iii) Copies and a list of documents or exhibits that it intends to introduce at the hearing; and (iv) A list identifying each witness who will testify on its behalf, including the witness's name, occupation, address, phone number, and a brief summary of the expected testimony.
claims.summary: A party must provide the opposing party and promptly file with the Administrative Law Judge the following information regarding the evidence it may present at the hearing: an outline or narrative summary of its case or defense, the legal theories upon which it will rely, copies and a list of documents or exhibits it intends to introduce at the hearing, and a list identifying each witness who will testify on its behalf.

claims.quote: Unless otherwise directed by the Administrative Law Judge, the disclosures required by paragraph (b)(1) of this section shall be made not later than 30 days before the date of the hearing.
claims.summary: The disclosures required by paragraph (b)(1) must be made not later than 30 days before the date of the hearing, unless otherwise directed by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: A party who intends to call an expert witness shall submit, in addition to the information required by paragraph (b)(1)(iv) of this section, a statement of the expert's qualifications, a list of other proceedings in which the expert has given expert testimony, and a list of publications authored or co-authored by the expert.
claims.summary: A party who intends to call an expert witness must submit a statement of the expert's qualifications, a list of other proceedings in which the expert has given expert testimony, and a list of publications authored or co-authored by the expert.
